אַֽל־תִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ ס כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר עֲשֽׂוּ־אִתִּ֤י בְרָכָה֙ וּצְא֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְאִכְל֤וּ אִישׁ־גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּאֵנָת֔וֹ וּשְׁת֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מֵי־בוֹרֽוֹ׃
until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.[^18]
עַד־בֹּאִ֕י וְלָקַחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם אֶ֤רֶץ דָּגָן֙ וְתִיר֔וֹשׁ אֶ֥רֶץ לֶ֖חֶם וּכְרָמִֽים׃
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, 'The LORD will rescue us.' Has any of the gods of the nations rescued his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
פֶּן־יַסִּ֨ית אֶתְכֶ֤ם חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֖ה יַצִּילֵ֑נוּ הַהִצִּ֜ילוּ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־אַרְצ֔וֹ מִיַּ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim?[^19] Did they rescue Samaria from my hand?
אַיֵּ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י חֲמָת֙ וְאַרְפָּ֔ד אַיֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י סְפַרְוָ֑יִם וְכִֽי־הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־שֹׁמְר֖וֹן מִיָּדִֽי׃
Who among all the gods of these lands has rescued his land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?"
מִ֗י בְּכָל־אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָֽאֲרָצוֹת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִ֑י כִּֽי־יַצִּ֧יל יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם מִיָּדִֽי׃
But they kept silent and did not answer him a word,[^20] for the king had commanded, "Do not answer him."
וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ וְלֹֽא־עָנ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ דָּבָ֑ר כִּֽי־מִצְוַ֨ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הִ֛יא לֵאמֹ֖ר לֹ֥א תַעֲנֻֽהוּ׃

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they told him the words of the Rabshakeh.

וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ אֲשֶׁר־עַל־הַ֠בַּיִת וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א הַסּוֹפֵ֜ר וְיוֹאָ֨ח בֶּן־אָסָ֧ף הַמַּזְכִּ֛יר אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י רַב שָׁקֵֽה׃ ס

n.1: In 701 BC. Chapters 36–39 are also found, with small differences, in 2 Kings 18:13–20:19, and parts of the story are told in 2 Chronicles 32. Where the Hebrew is the same, the English here follows the translation of 2 Kings. 2 Kings 18:14–16, Hezekiah's payment of tribute to Sennacherib, is not in Isaiah, and Hezekiah's psalm (38:9–20) is not in Kings.
n.2: Hebrew *rav-shaqeh*, from the Assyrian title *rab shaqe*, "chief cupbearer", a high official who here speaks for the king. Also in verses 4, 11–13 and 22. 2 Kings 18:17 says that the Tartan (the commander-in-chief) and the Rab-saris (the chief official) were sent with him.
n.3: A fortified city of Judah about 30 miles (50 km) southwest of Jerusalem, which Sennacherib was besieging.
n.4: Traditionally "the Fuller's Field", a field outside the city where cloth was washed and bleached. It is the place where Isaiah met Ahaz (7:3).
n.5: Literally "who was over the house", the title of the king's chief minister (22:15, 20–22). Also in verse 22.
n.6: Hebrew *mazkir*, "one who brings to remembrance": a senior royal official, perhaps the king's herald or the keeper of records. Also in verse 22.
n.7: Literally "I say: only a word of lips, counsel and strength for war." 2 Kings 18:20 reads "You say", that is, "You think that mere words are strategy and strength for war."
n.8: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.9: Hebrew *bamot*: places of worship, often on hilltops.
n.10: 2 Kings 18:22 reads "before this altar in Jerusalem".
n.11: Hebrew *pechah*, "governor".
n.12: 2 Kings 18:25 reads "against this place" in the first sentence.
n.13: The international language of diplomacy and trade in the Assyrian empire.
n.14: Literally "in Judean", that is, Hebrew. Also in verse 13.
n.15: The Hebrew text is written with coarse words for "dung" and "urine", but read with more polite ones, literally "excrement" and "the water of their feet".
n.16: 2 Kings 18:29 reads "from his hand", that is, from the hand of the king of Assyria.
n.17: Literally "Make a blessing with me", that is, surrender on terms.
n.18: 2 Kings 18:32 continues: "a land of olive trees and honey, so that you may live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah, for he is misleading you when he says, 'the LORD will rescue us.'"
n.19: Cities of Syria conquered by Assyria (10:9). 2 Kings 18:34 adds "Hena and Ivvah".
n.20: 2 Kings 18:36 reads "But the people kept silent".

v: When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.[^1]
וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־בְּגָדָ֑יו וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק וַיָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
He sent Eliakim the palace administrator,[^2] Shebna the secretary and the senior priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת־אֶלְיָקִ֨ים אֲשֶׁר־עַל־הַבַּ֜יִת וְאֵ֣ת ׀ שֶׁבְנָ֣א הַסּוֹפֵ֗ר וְאֵת֙ זִקְנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים אֶל־יְשַֽׁעְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־אָמ֖וֹץ הַנָּבִֽיא׃
They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, of rebuke and of disgrace. Children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to deliver them.
וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ יוֹם־צָרָ֧ה וְתוֹכֵחָ֛ה וּנְאָצָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י בָ֤אוּ בָנִים֙ עַד־מַשְׁבֵּ֔ר וְכֹ֥חַ אַ֖יִן לְלֵדָֽה׃

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh,[^3] whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. So pray for the remnant that is left."

אוּלַ֡י יִשְׁמַע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֵ֣ת ׀ דִּבְרֵ֣י רַב־[t] שָׁקֵ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שְׁלָח֨וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֤וּר ׀ אֲדֹנָיו֙ לְחָרֵף֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַ֔י וְהוֹכִ֙יחַ֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖ע יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְנָשָׂ֣אתָ תְפִלָּ֔ה בְּעַ֥ד הַשְּׁאֵרִ֖ית הַנִּמְצָאָֽה׃
When King Hezekiah's servants came to Isaiah,
וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַבְדֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶל־יְשַׁעְיָֽהוּ׃
Isaiah said to them, "Say this to your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the king of Assyria's lackeys[^4] have insulted me.

וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן אֶל־אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֑ם כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־תִּירָא֙ מִפְּנֵ֤י הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר גִּדְּפ֛וּ נַעֲרֵ֥י מֶלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֖וּר אוֹתִֽי׃
I am going to put a spirit in him, so that he will hear a rumor and go back to his own land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.'"
הִנְנִ֨י נוֹתֵ֥ן בּוֹ֙ ר֔וּחַ וְשָׁמַ֥ע שְׁמוּעָ֖ה וְשָׁ֣ב אֶל־אַרְצ֑וֹ וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃
The Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ רַב־שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּמְצָא֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר נִלְחָ֖ם עַל־לִבְנָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י נָסַ֖ע מִלָּכִֽישׁ׃
Then the king heard that Tirhakah king of Cush[^5] had set out to fight against him. When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,[^6]
וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע עַל־תִּרְהָ֤קָה מֶֽלֶךְ־כּוּשׁ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יָצָ֖א לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם אִתָּ֑ךְ וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃
"Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'
כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־יַשִּֽׁאֲךָ֣ אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בּוֹטֵ֥חַ בּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, destroying them completely.[^7] And will you be rescued?
הִנֵּ֣ה ׀ אַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֜וּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר לְכָל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת לְהַחֲרִימָ֑ם וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּנָּצֵֽל׃
Did the gods of the nations that my predecessors[^8] destroyed rescue them, the nations of Gozan, Haran and Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
הַהִצִּ֨ילוּ אוֹתָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִשְׁחִ֣יתוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֶת־גּוֹזָ֖ן וְאֶת־חָרָ֑ן וְרֶ֥צֶף וּבְנֵי־עֶ֖דֶן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּתְלַשָּֽׂר׃
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena and of Ivvah?"
אַיֵּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־חֲמָת֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַרְפָּ֔ד וּמֶ֖לֶךְ לָעִ֣יר סְפַרְוָ֑יִם הֵנַ֖ע וְעִוָּֽה׃
Hezekiah took the letter[^9] from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the LORD, and Hezekiah spread it out before the LORD.
וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ אֶת־הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֙עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD and said,
וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
"The LORD of Armies,[^10] the God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim,[^11] you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אַתָּה־ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Turn your ear, LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear all the words that Sennacherib has sent to mock the living God.
הַטֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה ׀ אָזְנְךָ֙ וּֽשְׁמָ֔ע פְּקַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה עֵינֶ֖ךָ וּרְאֵ֑ה וּשְׁמַ֗ע אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י סַנְחֵרִ֔יב אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֔ח לְחָרֵ֖ף אֱלֹהִ֥ים חָֽי׃
It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the countries and their lands.[^12]
אָמְנָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה הֶחֱרִ֜יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת־כָּל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת וְאֶת־אַרְצָֽם׃
They have thrown their gods into the fire, for they were not gods but only the work of human hands, wood and stone. So they destroyed them.
וְנָתֹ֥ן אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם בָּאֵ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֣י אִם־מַעֲשֵׂ֧ה יְדֵֽי־אָדָ֛ם עֵ֥ץ וָאֶ֖בֶן וַֽיְאַבְּדֽוּם׃
Now, LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the LORD."[^13]
וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ מִיָד֑וֹ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria,[^14]
וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ הִתְפַּלַּ֣לְתָּ אֵלַ֔י אֶל־סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
this is the word that the LORD has spoken against him: The virgin Daughter Zion[^15] despises you and mocks you. Daughter Jerusalem tosses her head behind your back.
זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן אַחֲרֶ֙יךָ֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הֵנִ֔יעָה בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Whom have you mocked and insulted? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!
אֶת־מִ֤י חֵרַ֙פְתָּ֙ וְגִדַּ֔פְתָּ וְעַל־מִ֖י הֲרִימ֣וֹתָה קּ֑וֹל וַתִּשָּׂ֥א מָר֛וֹם עֵינֶ֖יךָ אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

Through your servants you have mocked the Lord.[^16] You have said, 'With my many chariots I have gone up to the heights of the mountains, to the farthest reaches of Lebanon. I cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest junipers. I came to its farthest heights, its densest forest.[^17]

בְּיַ֣ד עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ חֵרַ֣פְתָּ ׀ אֲדֹנָי֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרֹ֥ב רִכְבִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י עָלִ֛יתִי מְר֥וֹם הָרִ֖ים יַרְכְּתֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְאֶכְרֹ֞ת קוֹמַ֤ת אֲרָזָיו֙ מִבְחַ֣ר בְּרֹשָׁ֔יו וְאָבוֹא֙ מְר֣וֹם קִצּ֔וֹ יַ֖עַר כַּרְמִלּֽוֹ׃
I dug wells and drank water,[^18] and with the soles of my feet I dried up all the streams of Egypt.'[^19]
אֲנִ֥י קַ֖רְתִּי וְשָׁתִ֣יתִי מָ֑יִם וְאַחְרִב֙ בְּכַף־פְּעָמַ֔י כֹּ֖ל יְאֹרֵ֥י מָצֽוֹר׃
Have you not heard? Long ago I planned it.[^20] From days of old I formed it. Now I have brought it about, that you should turn fortified cities into heaps of ruins.
הֲלֽוֹא־שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵאתִ֔יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לְהַשְׁא֛וֹת גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֽוֹת׃

Their people, drained of strength,[^21] are dismayed and put to shame. They are like plants of the field and tender green shoots, like grass on the rooftops, like a field before the grain is grown.[^22]
וְיֹֽשְׁבֵיהֶן֙ קִצְרֵי־יָ֔ד חַ֖תּוּ וָבֹ֑שׁוּ הָי֞וּ עֵ֤שֶׂב שָׂדֶה֙ וִ֣ירַק דֶּ֔שֶׁא חֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֔וֹת וּשְׁדֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י קָמָֽה׃
I know when you sit down, when you go out and when you come in, and how you rage against me.
וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ וְצֵאתְךָ֥ וּבוֹאֲךָ֖ יָדָ֑עְתִּי וְאֵ֖ת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ֥ אֵלָֽי׃
Because you rage against me and your arrogance has reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will turn you back by the way you came.
יַ֚עַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ֣ אֵלַ֔י וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ֖ עָלָ֣ה בְאָזְנָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁ֣יבֹתִ֔יךָ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אתָ בָּֽהּ׃

And this will be the sign for you:[^23] This year you will eat what grows by itself, and in the second year what springs up from that. But in the third year, sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת אָכ֤וֹל הַשָּׁנָה֙ סָפִ֔יחַ וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית שָׁחִ֑יס וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗ית זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים *ואכול **וְאִכְל֥וּ פִרְיָֽם׃
The survivors of the house of Judah who are left will again take root below and bear fruit above.
וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית־יְהוּדָ֛ה הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ לְמָ֑טָּה וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י לְמָֽעְלָה׃
For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will do this.
כִּ֤י מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תֵּצֵ֣א שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה מֵהַ֣ר צִיּ֑וֹן קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־זֹּֽאת׃ ס

Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria: He will not come into this city or shoot an arrow there. He will not come before it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לֹ֤א יָבוֹא֙ אֶל־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹֽא־יוֹרֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם חֵ֑ץ וְלֹֽא־יְקַדְּמֶ֣נָּה מָגֵ֔ן וְלֹֽא־יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ עֳלֶ֖יהָ סֹלְלָֽה׃
By the way that he came, he will go back. He will not come into this city, declares the LORD.
בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖א בָּ֣הּ יָשׁ֑וּב וְאֶל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."
וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃ ס
Then the angel[^24] of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 in the camp of Assyria. When people got up early in the morning, there were all the dead bodies.
וַיֵּצֵ֣א ׀ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּכֶּה֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה אַשּׁ֔וּר מֵאָ֛ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֥ה כֻלָּ֖ם פְּגָרִ֥ים מֵתִֽים׃
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and went back home, and he stayed in Nineveh.
וַיִּסַּ֣ע וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖שָׁב סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּנִֽינְוֵֽה׃

One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat.[^25] And his son Esarhaddon became king in his place.

וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית ׀ נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר בָּנָיו֙ הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. "The house of the LORD" is the temple. This chapter is also found in 2 Kings 19:1–37.
n.2: Literally "who was over the house" (36:3).
n.3: On this title, see 36:2. 2 Kings 19:4 reads "all the words".
n.4: Hebrew *na'arim*, "young men, servants", here probably said with contempt.
n.5: The region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia). Its kings then also ruled Egypt.
n.6: 2 Kings 19:9 reads "So he again sent messengers".
n.7: Hebrew *charam*: to destroy completely, as something devoted to a god (34:2).
n.8: Literally "my fathers".
n.9: Literally "the letters". The Hebrew then says "and read it … and spread it out".
n.10: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verse 32. 2 Kings 19:15 reads only "the LORD".
n.11: Winged creatures whose images were on the cover of the ark and in the inner sanctuary of the temple (Exodus 25:18–22; 1 Kings 6:23–28).
n.12: Literally "all the lands and their land". 2 Kings 19:17 reads "the nations and their land".
n.13: 2 Kings 19:19 reads "that you, LORD, alone are God".
n.14: 2 Kings 19:20 reads "I have heard what you prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria."
n.15: A poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman (1:8).
n.16: Hebrew *Adonai*, "the Lord", not the name YHWH. 2 Kings 19:23 reads "Through your messengers".
n.17: Literally "the forest of its *karmel*", its fruitful land or orchard. 2 Kings 19:23 reads "its farthest lodging place" instead of "its farthest heights".
n.18: 2 Kings 19:24 reads "foreign waters".
n.19: Hebrew *Matsor*, a poetic name for Egypt (19:6). Literally "all the Nile streams of Matsor".
n.20: Literally "From far off I did it".
n.22: Hebrew *shedemah*, "field" or "terrace". 2 Kings 19:26 reads *shedefah*, "scorched", which differs by one letter: "scorched before it is grown".
n.23: The prophet now speaks to Hezekiah.
n.24: Or "messenger". Hebrew *mal'akh* means both. 2 Kings 19:35 begins "That night".
n.25: Urartu, a kingdom in what is now Armenia and eastern Turkey. Sennacherib was killed in 681 BC.

v: In those days Hezekiah became ill and was at the point of death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said to him, "This is what the LORD[^1] says: Give instructions to your household,[^2] for you are going to die. You will not recover."
בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לָמ֑וּת וַיָּב֣וֹא אֵ֠לָיו יְשַׁעְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־אָמ֜וֹץ הַנָּבִ֗יא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ צַ֣ו לְבֵיתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י מֵ֥ת אַתָּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִֽחְיֶֽה׃
Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
וַיַּסֵּ֧ב חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ פָּנָ֖יו אֶל־הַקִּ֑יר וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
He said, "Please, LORD, remember how I have walked before you faithfully and with my whole heart, and have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
וַיֹּאמַ֗ר אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ זְכָר־נָ֞א אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנֶ֗יךָ בֶּֽאֱמֶת֙ וּבְלֵ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם וְהַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עָשִׂ֑יתִי וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל׃ ס
Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:[^3]
וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃
"Go and say to Hezekiah, 'This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor[^4] David, says: I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. I am going to add fifteen years to your life.

הָל֞וֹךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔יךָ שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־תְּפִלָּתֶ֔ךָ רָאִ֖יתִי אֶת־דִּמְעָתֶ֑ךָ הִנְנִי֙ יוֹסִ֣ף עַל־יָמֶ֔יךָ חֲמֵ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה׃
I will rescue you and this city from the power of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.[^5]
וּמִכַּ֤ף מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁוּר֙ אַצִּ֣ילְךָ֔ וְאֵ֖ת הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וְגַנּוֹתִ֖י עַל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּֽאת׃
This is the sign to you from the LORD that the LORD will do what he has promised:[^6]
וְזֶה־לְּךָ֥ הָא֖וֹת מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃
I am going to make the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz,[^7] which has gone down with the sun, go back ten steps.'" So the sun went back ten steps on the stairway it had gone down.
הִנְנִ֣י מֵשִׁ֣יב אֶת־צֵ֣ל הַֽמַּעֲל֡וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרְדָה֩ בְמַעֲל֨וֹת אָחָ֥ז בַּשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ אֲחֹרַנִּ֖ית עֶ֣שֶׂר מַעֲל֑וֹת וַתָּ֤שָׁב הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר מַעֲל֔וֹת בַּֽמַּעֲל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָרָֽדָה׃ ס
A writing[^8] of Hezekiah king of Judah, after he had been ill and had recovered from his illness:
מִכְתָּ֖ב לְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה בַּחֲלֹת֕וֹ וַיְחִ֖י מֵחָלְיֽוֹ׃
I said, "In the prime of my days[^9] I must go through the gates of Sheol;[^10] I am robbed of the rest of my years."[^11]
אֲנִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי בִּדְמִ֥י יָמַ֛י אֵלֵ֖כָה בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֣י שְׁא֑וֹל פֻּקַּ֖דְתִּי יֶ֥תֶר שְׁנוֹתָֽי׃
I said, "I will not see the LORD,[^12] the LORD in the land of the living. I will no longer look on any human being, when I am among those who live where life has ceased."[^13]
אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ לֹא־אֶרְאֶ֣ה יָ֔הּ יָ֖הּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הַחַיִּ֑ים לֹא־אַבִּ֥יט אָדָ֛ם ע֖וֹד עִם־י֥וֹשְׁבֵי חָֽדֶל׃
My dwelling[^14] is pulled up and taken away from me like a shepherd's tent. Like a weaver I have rolled up my life; he cuts me off from the loom.[^15] From day to night you bring me to an end.[^16]
דּוֹרִ֗י נִסַּ֧ע וְנִגְלָ֛ה מִנִּ֖י כְּאֹ֣הֶל רֹעִ֑י קִפַּ֨דְתִּי כָאֹרֵ֤ג חַיַּי֙ מִדַּלָּ֣ה יְבַצְּעֵ֔נִי מִיּ֥וֹם עַד־לַ֖יְלָה תַּשְׁלִימֵֽנִי׃
I composed myself until morning,[^17] but like a lion he breaks all my bones. From day to night you bring me to an end.
שִׁוִּ֤יתִי עַד־בֹּ֙קֶר֙ כּֽ͏ָאֲרִ֔י כֵּ֥ן יְשַׁבֵּ֖ר כָּל־עַצְמוֹתָ֑י מִיּ֥וֹם עַד־לַ֖יְלָה תַּשְׁלִימֵֽנִי׃
Like a swift or a thrush[^18] I chirp; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weak from looking upward. Lord,[^19] I am oppressed; be my security![^20]
כְּס֤וּס עָגוּר֙ כֵּ֣ן אֲצַפְצֵ֔ף אֶהְגֶּ֖ה כַּיּוֹנָ֑ה דַּלּ֤וּ עֵינַי֙ לַמָּר֔וֹם אֲדֹנָ֖י עָֽשְׁקָה־לִּ֥י עָרְבֵֽנִי׃
What can I say? He has spoken to me, and he himself has done it. I will walk slowly[^21] all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
מָֽה־אֲדַבֵּ֥ר וְאָֽמַר־לִ֖י וְה֣וּא עָשָׂ֑ה אֶדַּדֶּ֥ה כָל־שְׁנוֹתַ֖י עַל־מַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃
Lord, by these things people live, and in all of them is the life of my spirit. You restore my health and let me live![^22]
אֲדֹנָ֖י עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יִֽחְי֑וּ וּלְכָל־בָּהֶן֙ חַיֵּ֣י רוּחִ֔י וְתַחֲלִימֵ֖נִי וְהַחֲיֵֽנִי׃
Look, it was for my good that I had such bitter grief.[^23] In your love you have kept my life from the pit of destruction,[^24] for you have thrown all my sins behind your back.
הִנֵּ֥ה לְשָׁל֖וֹם מַר־לִ֣י מָ֑ר וְאַתָּ֞ה חָשַׁ֤קְתָּ נַפְשִׁי֙ מִשַּׁ֣חַת בְּלִ֔י כִּ֥י הִשְׁלַ֛כְתָּ אַחֲרֵ֥י גֵוְךָ֖ כָּל־חֲטָאָֽי׃
For Sheol cannot thank you; death cannot praise you. Those who go down to the Pit[^25] cannot hope for your faithfulness.
כִּ֣י לֹ֥א שְׁא֛וֹל תּוֹדֶ֖ךָּ מָ֣וֶת יְהַלְלֶ֑ךָּ לֹֽא־יְשַׂבְּר֥וּ יֽוֹרְדֵי־ב֖וֹר אֶל־אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃
The living, the living, they thank you, as I do today. Fathers make known your faithfulness to their children.
חַ֥י חַ֛י ה֥וּא יוֹדֶ֖ךָ כָּמ֣וֹנִי הַיּ֑וֹם אָ֣ב לְבָנִ֔ים יוֹדִ֖יעַ אֶל־אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃
The LORD will save me,[^26] and we will play my songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD.
יְהוָ֖ה לְהוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נִי וּנְגִנוֹתַ֧י נְנַגֵּ֛ן כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּ֖ינוּ עַל־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
Isaiah said, "Let them take a cake of figs and spread it on the boil, and he will recover."[^27]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ יִשְׂא֖וּ דְּבֶ֣לֶת תְּאֵנִ֑ים וְיִמְרְח֥וּ עַֽל־הַשְּׁחִ֖ין וְיֶֽחִי׃
And Hezekiah said, "What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מָ֣ה א֑וֹת כִּ֥י אֶעֱלֶ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Verses 1–8 and 21–22 are also found, with differences, in 2 Kings 20:1–11. Hezekiah's psalm (verses 9–20) is found only in Isaiah.
n.2: Literally "Command your house".
n.3: 2 Kings 20:4 reads "Isaiah had not yet gone out of the middle courtyard when the word of the LORD came to him".
n.4: Literally "your father". 2 Kings 20:5–6 adds "the ruler of my people" after "Hezekiah", and "I am going to heal you. On the third day you will go up to the house of the LORD" before "I am going to add".
n.5: 2 Kings 20:6 adds "for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David" (as in 37:35).
n.6: In 2 Kings 20:8–11 Hezekiah first asks for a sign (compare verse 22), and Isaiah lets him choose whether the shadow will go forward or back.
n.7: Literally "the shadow of the steps, which has gone down on the steps of Ahaz". The "steps" were probably those of a stairway whose shadow marked the time of day. The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) reads "the steps of the upper room of Ahaz" (compare 2 Kings 23:12).
n.8: Hebrew *mikhtav*. Some scholars read *miktam*, a term found in the titles of Psalms 16 and 56–60, with a small change to the Hebrew. The psalm in verses 10–20 has many rare words, and its meaning is uncertain in places.
n.9: Hebrew *bidmi yamai*, perhaps "in the quiet of my days" or "in the middle of my days" (compare Psalm 102:25; 102:24 in most English Bibles).
n.10: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. Also in verse 18.
n.11: Or "I am consigned there for the rest of my years".
n.12: *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH (12:2).
n.13: Literally "with the inhabitants of cessation". Some scholars read *cheled*, "the world", with a small change to the Hebrew: "with those who live in the world".
n.14: Hebrew *dor*, usually "generation", here probably "dwelling".
n.15: Literally "from the thrum", the threads that held the woven cloth to the loom. The weaver cut them when the cloth was finished.
n.16: That is, between morning and evening, before the day is out. Also in verse 13.
n.17: Or "I waited quietly until morning". Some scholars read *shivva'ti*, "I cried for help", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.18: Hebrew *sus agur*. *Sus* (written for *sis*) and *agur* are birds named together in Jeremiah 8:7. Their identification is uncertain.
n.19: Hebrew *Adonai*, "the Lord", not the name YHWH. Also in verse 16.
n.20: Literally "Lord, oppression is mine; stand surety for me!", that is, take up my debt and my cause.
n.21: Hebrew *eddaddeh*, perhaps "I will walk humbly" or "I will wander". The meaning is uncertain.
n.22: The Hebrew of this verse is very difficult. Literally "Lord, on them they live, and for all in them the life of my spirit, and you restore me and make me live." It may also be read as a prayer: "Restore my health and let me live!"
n.23: Literally "Look, for peace it was bitter to me, bitter".
n.24: Literally "you loved my life from the pit of nothingness".
n.25: Hebrew *bor*, "pit, cistern", a name for the grave and the world of the dead.
n.26: Literally "The LORD, to save me", perhaps "The LORD is ready to save me".
n.27: Verses 21–22 are found in 2 Kings 20:7–8, where they come before the sign of the shadow, after verse 6 here. 2 Kings 20:7 reads "Then Isaiah said, 'Bring a cake of figs.' They brought it and put it on the boil, and he recovered." 2 Kings 20:8 reads "What will be the sign that the LORD will heal me and that I will go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?"

v: At that time Merodach-baladan[^1] son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that he had been ill and had recovered.[^2]
בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֡וא שָׁלַ֡ח מְרֹדַ֣ךְ בַּ֠לְאֲדָן בֶּֽן־בַּלְאֲדָ֧ן מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל סְפָרִ֥ים וּמִנְחָ֖ה אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ וַיִּשְׁמַ֕ע כִּ֥י חָלָ֖ה וֽ͏ַיֶּחֱזָֽק׃

Hezekiah was glad because of them[^3] and showed them his treasure house: the silver, the gold, the spices and the fine oil, his whole armory,[^4] and everything that was found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his palace or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.

וַיִּשְׂמַ֣ח עֲלֵיהֶם֮ חִזְקִיָּהוּ֒ וַיַּרְאֵ֣ם אֶת־בֵּ֣ית *נכתה **נְכֹת֡וֹ אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף֩ וְאֶת־הַזָּהָ֨ב וְאֶת־הַבְּשָׂמִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת ׀ הַשֶּׁ֣מֶן הַטּ֗וֹב וְאֵת֙ כָּל־בֵּ֣ית כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִמְצָ֖א בְּאֹֽצְרֹתָ֑יו לֹֽא־הָיָ֣ה דָבָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־הֶרְאָ֧ם חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּבֵית֖וֹ וּבְכָל־מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃
Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say? And where did they come to you from?" Hezekiah said, "They came to me from a distant land, from Babylon."

וַיָּבֹא֙ יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו מָ֥ה אָמְר֣וּ ׀ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וּמֵאַ֙יִן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ מֵאֶ֧רֶץ רְחוֹקָ֛ה בָּ֥אוּ אֵלַ֖י מִבָּבֶֽל׃
He asked, "What did they see in your palace?" Hezekiah said, "They saw everything in my palace. There is nothing in my treasuries that I did not show them."
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֥ה רָא֖וּ בְּבֵיתֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּבֵיתִי֙ רָא֔וּ לֹֽא־הָיָ֥ה דָבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־הִרְאִיתִ֖ים בְּאוֹצְרֹתָֽי׃
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD of Armies.[^5]
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
The days are coming when everything in your palace, and all that your ancestors have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
הִנֵּה֮ יָמִ֣ים בָּאִים֒ וְנִשָּׂ֣א ׀ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵיתֶ֗ךָ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר אָצְר֧וּ אֲבֹתֶ֛יךָ עַד־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה בָּבֶ֑ל לֹֽא־יִוָּתֵ֥ר דָּבָ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
And some of your sons, your own descendants whom you will father, will be taken away, and they will be officials[^6] in the palace of the king of Babylon."
וּמִבָּנֶ֜יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵצְא֧וּ מִמְּךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תּוֹלִ֖יד יִקָּ֑חוּ וְהָיוּ֙ סָרִיסִ֔ים בְּהֵיכַ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." For he thought,[^7] "There will be peace and security in my days."
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶֽל־יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ ט֥וֹב דְּבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י יִהְיֶ֛ה שָׁל֥וֹם וֶאֱמֶ֖ת בְּיָמָֽי׃ פ

n.1: Marduk-apla-iddina II, who ruled Babylon in 722–710 and again in 703 BC. He was a long-time enemy of Assyria and was probably looking for allies. 2 Kings 20:12 calls him Berodach-baladan. This chapter is also found in 2 Kings 20:12–19.
n.2: 2 Kings 20:12 does not have "and had recovered".
n.3: 2 Kings 20:13 reads "Hezekiah listened to them".
n.4: Literally "all the house of his equipment".
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. 2 Kings 20:16 reads "the word of the LORD".
n.6: Hebrew *sarisim*, court officials. The word can also mean eunuchs.
n.7: Literally "For he said". 2 Kings 20:19 reads "For he said, 'Is it not good, if there will be peace and security in my days?'" *Security* is literally "truth" or "faithfulness".

v: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.[^1]
נַחֲמ֥וּ נַחֲמ֖וּ עַמִּ֑י יֹאמַ֖ר אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
Speak tenderly to Jerusalem,[^2] and call out to her that her hard service is over,[^3] that her guilt has been paid for, that she has received from the hand of the LORD[^4] double for all her sins.
דַּבְּר֞וּ עַל־לֵ֤ב יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ וְקִרְא֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֤י מָֽלְאָה֙ צְבָאָ֔הּ כִּ֥י נִרְצָ֖ה עֲוֺנָ֑הּ כִּ֤י לָקְחָה֙ מִיַּ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה כִּפְלַ֖יִם בְּכָל־חַטֹּאתֶֽיהָ׃ ס
A voice is shouting: "In the wilderness prepare the way for the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.[^5]
ק֣וֹל קוֹרֵ֔א בַּמִּדְבָּ֕ר פַּנּ֖וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֑ה יַשְּׁרוּ֙ בָּעֲרָבָ֔ה מְסִלָּ֖ה לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
Every valley will be raised up, and every mountain and hill made low. The uneven ground will become level, and the rugged places a plain.
כָּל־גֶּיא֙ יִנָּשֵׂ֔א וְכָל־הַ֥ר וְגִבְעָ֖ה יִשְׁפָּ֑לוּ וְהָיָ֤ה הֶֽעָקֹב֙ לְמִישׁ֔וֹר וְהָרְכָסִ֖ים לְבִקְעָֽה׃
Then the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all people[^6] will see it together. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken."
וְנִגְלָ֖ה כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֑ה וְרָא֤וּ כָל־בָּשָׂר֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ ס
A voice says, "Shout!" And I said,[^7] "What shall I shout?" All people are grass, and all their faithfulness[^8] is like the flower of the field.
ק֚וֹל אֹמֵ֣ר קְרָ֔א וְאָמַ֖ר מָ֣ה אֶקְרָ֑א כָּל־הַבָּשָׂ֣ר חָצִ֔יר וְכָל־חַסְדּ֖וֹ כְּצִ֥יץ הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
The grass withers, the flower fades, when the breath[^9] of the LORD blows on it. Surely the people are grass.
יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֔יץ כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה נָ֣שְׁבָה בּ֑וֹ אָכֵ֥ן חָצִ֖יר הָעָֽם׃
The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.[^10]
יָבֵ֥שׁ חָצִ֖יר נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֑יץ וּדְבַר־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יָק֥וּם לְעוֹלָֽם׃ ס

Go up on a high mountain, you who bring good news to Zion![^11] Raise your voice with strength, you who bring good news to Jerusalem! Raise it; do not be afraid! Say to the towns of Judah, "Here is your God!"
עַ֣ל הַר־גָּבֹ֤הַ עֲלִי־לָךְ֙ מְבַשֶּׂ֣רֶת צִיּ֔וֹן הָרִ֤ימִי בַכֹּ֙חַ֙ קוֹלֵ֔ךְ מְבַשֶּׂ֖רֶת יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם הָרִ֙ימִי֙ אַל־תִּירָ֔אִי אִמְרִי֙ לְעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה הִנֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
Look, the Lord GOD comes with might, and his arm rules for him. Look, his reward is with him, and his recompense goes before him.[^12]
הִנֵּ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ בְּחָזָ֣ק יָב֔וֹא וּזְרֹע֖וֹ מֹ֣שְׁלָה ל֑וֹ הִנֵּ֤ה שְׂכָרוֹ֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וּפְעֻלָּת֖וֹ לְפָנָֽיו׃
Like a shepherd he tends his flock. He gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them close to his heart;[^13] he gently leads the ewes that have young.
כְּרֹעֶה֙ עֶדְר֣וֹ יִרְעֶ֔ה בִּזְרֹעוֹ֙ יְקַבֵּ֣ץ טְלָאִ֔ים וּבְחֵיק֖וֹ יִשָּׂ֑א עָל֖וֹת יְנַהֵֽל׃ ס

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the heavens with the span of his hand?[^14] Who has held the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains on scales and the hills in a balance?
מִֽי־מָדַ֨ד בְּשָׁעֳל֜וֹ מַ֗יִם וְשָׁמַ֙יִם֙ בַּזֶּ֣רֶת תִּכֵּ֔ן וְכָ֥ל בַּשָּׁלִ֖שׁ עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשָׁקַ֤ל בַּפֶּ֙לֶס֙ הָרִ֔ים וּגְבָע֖וֹת בְּמֹאזְנָֽיִם׃
Who has measured the Spirit[^15] of the LORD, or instructed him as his counselor?[^16]
מִֽי־תִכֵּ֥ן אֶת־ר֖וּחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְאִ֥ישׁ עֲצָת֖וֹ יוֹדִיעֶֽנּוּ׃
Whom did he consult to give him understanding? Who taught him the path of justice, taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
אֶת־מִ֤י נוֹעָץ֙ וַיְבִינֵ֔הוּ וַֽיְלַמְּדֵ֖הוּ בְּאֹ֣רַח מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וַיְלַמְּדֵ֣הוּ דַ֔עַת וְדֶ֥רֶךְ תְּבוּנ֖וֹת יוֹדִיעֶֽנּוּ׃
Look, the nations are like a drop from a bucket; they are counted as dust on the scales. Look, he lifts up the coastlands[^17] like fine dust.
הֵ֤ן גּוֹיִם֙ כְּמַ֣ר מִדְּלִ֔י וּכְשַׁ֥חַק מֹאזְנַ֖יִם נֶחְשָׁ֑בוּ הֵ֥ן אִיִּ֖ים כַּדַּ֥ק יִטּֽוֹל׃
Lebanon is not enough for fuel, nor are its animals enough for a burnt offering.
וּלְבָנ֕וֹן אֵ֥ין דֵּ֖י בָּעֵ֑ר וְחַיָת֔וֹ אֵ֥ין דֵּ֖י עוֹלָֽה׃ ס
All the nations are as nothing before him; he counts them as less than nothing and emptiness.[^18]
כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם כְּאַ֣יִן נֶגְדּ֑וֹ מֵאֶ֥פֶס וָתֹ֖הוּ נֶחְשְׁבוּ־לֽוֹ׃
To whom, then, will you compare God?[^19] What likeness will you set beside him?
וְאֶל־מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן אֵ֑ל וּמַה־דְּמ֖וּת תַּ֥עַרְכוּ לֽוֹ׃
An idol? A craftsman casts it, and a goldsmith overlays it with gold and casts silver chains for it.
הַפֶּ֙סֶל֙ נָסַ֣ךְ חָרָ֔שׁ וְצֹרֵ֖ף בַּזָּהָ֣ב יְרַקְּעֶ֑נּוּ וּרְתֻק֥וֹת כֶּ֖סֶף צוֹרֵֽף׃
One too poor for such an offering[^20] chooses wood that will not rot. He looks for a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.
הַֽמְסֻכָּ֣ן תְּרוּמָ֔ה עֵ֥ץ לֹֽא־יִרְקַ֖ב יִבְחָ֑ר חָרָ֤שׁ חָכָם֙ יְבַקֶּשׁ־ל֔וֹ לְהָכִ֥ין פֶּ֖סֶל לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט׃
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood how the earth was founded?[^21]
הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ הֲל֣וֹא תִשְׁמָ֔עוּ הֲל֛וֹא הֻגַּ֥ד מֵרֹ֖אשׁ לָכֶ֑ם הֲלוֹא֙ הֲבִ֣ינֹתֶ֔ם מוֹסְד֖וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

He is the one who sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain[^22] and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
הַיֹּשֵׁב֙ עַל־ח֣וּג הָאָ֔רֶץ וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כַּחֲגָבִ֑ים הַנּוֹטֶ֤ה כַדֹּק֙ שָׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמְתָּחֵ֥ם כָּאֹ֖הֶל לָשָֽׁבֶת׃
He brings rulers to nothing and makes the judges of the earth like emptiness.
הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן רוֹזְנִ֖ים לְאָ֑יִן שֹׁ֥פְטֵי אֶ֖רֶץ כַּתֹּ֥הוּ עָשָֽׂה׃
Scarcely are they planted, scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stem taken root in the ground, when he blows on them and they wither, and the storm carries them off like straw.
אַ֣ף בַּל־נִטָּ֗עוּ אַ֚ף בַּל־זֹרָ֔עוּ אַ֛ף בַּל־שֹׁרֵ֥שׁ בָּאָ֖רֶץ גִּזְעָ֑ם וְגַם־נָשַׁ֤ף בָּהֶם֙ וַיִּבָ֔שׁוּ וּסְעָרָ֖ה כַּקַּ֥שׁ תִּשָּׂאֵֽם׃ ס
To whom, then, will you compare me, that I should be like him? says the Holy One.
וְאֶל־מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי וְאֶשְׁוֶ֑ה יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ׃
Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He brings out their army[^23] by number and calls them all by name. Because of his great strength and mighty power, not one of them is missing.
שְׂאוּ־מָר֨וֹם עֵינֵיכֶ֤ם וּרְאוּ֙ מִי־בָרָ֣א אֵ֔לֶּה הַמּוֹצִ֥יא בְמִסְפָּ֖ר צְבָאָ֑ם לְכֻלָּם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יִקְרָ֔א מֵרֹ֤ב אוֹנִים֙ וְאַמִּ֣יץ כֹּ֔חַ אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֥א נֶעְדָּֽר׃ ס
Why do you say, Jacob, and why do you declare, Israel, "My way is hidden from the LORD, and my God pays no attention to my cause"?[^24]
לָ֤מָּה תֹאמַר֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּתְדַבֵּ֖ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נִסְתְּרָ֤ה דַרְכִּי֙ מֵֽיְהוָ֔ה וּמֵאֱלֹהַ֖י מִשְׁפָּטִ֥י יַעֲבֽוֹר׃
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not grow tired or weary; his understanding cannot be searched out.
הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם־לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֱלֹהֵ֨י עוֹלָ֤ם ׀ יְהוָה֙ בּוֹרֵא֙ קְצ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ לֹ֥א יִיעַ֖ף וְלֹ֣א יִיגָ֑ע אֵ֥ין חֵ֖קֶר לִתְבוּנָתֽוֹ׃
He gives strength to the weary, and to those who have no power he gives great might.
נֹתֵ֥ן לַיָּעֵ֖ף כֹּ֑חַ וּלְאֵ֥ין אוֹנִ֖ים עָצְמָ֥ה יַרְבֶּֽה׃
Even young men grow tired and weary, and strong young men stumble and fall.
וְיִֽעֲפ֥וּ נְעָרִ֖ים וְיִגָ֑עוּ וּבַחוּרִ֖ים כָּשׁ֥וֹל יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ׃
But those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will rise up on wings like eagles;[^25] they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not grow tired.
וְקוֹיֵ֤ יְהוָה֙ יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ יַעֲל֥וּ אֵ֖בֶר כַּנְּשָׁרִ֑ים יָר֙וּצוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִיגָ֔עוּ יֵלְכ֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יִיעָֽפוּ׃ פ

n.1: *Comfort* is plural: the command is given to more than one, perhaps the prophets or the heavenly council (6:8). The Septuagint adds "Priests" at the start of verse 2. Chapters 40–66 speak to the people of Judah in exile in Babylon and after their return. They name Cyrus of Persia, who conquered Babylon in 539 BC (44:28; 45:1). Many scholars attribute them to a later prophet or prophets in the tradition of Isaiah; traditionally they have been read as the words of Isaiah son of Amoz.
n.2: Literally "Speak to the heart of Jerusalem", as one speaks to win someone's love or to comfort them (Genesis 34:3; Ruth 2:13).
n.3: Literally "that her term of service is fulfilled". Hebrew *tsava*, "army, military service, forced labor" (Job 7:1).
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: The Hebrew accents join "in the wilderness" to "prepare". The Septuagint joins it to the voice: "A voice of one shouting in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God." The Gospels quote this verse from the Septuagint, applying it to John the Baptizer (Matthew 3:3; Mark 1:3; Luke 3:4–6; John 1:23). In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, YHWH ("the LORD").
n.6: Literally "all flesh". Also in verse 6. The Septuagint reads "and all flesh will see the salvation of God", quoted in Luke 3:6.
n.7: The vowels of the Hebrew text read "And he said" or "And someone said". The same consonants can be read "And I said", as the Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) and the Septuagint understood them.
n.8: Hebrew *chesed*, "faithful love", here perhaps the loyalty or the goodness of human beings. The Septuagint reads "all the glory of a human being". 1 Peter 1:24–25 quotes verses 6–8 from the Septuagint.
n.9: Or "wind". Hebrew *ruach*. The Septuagint has the line "The grass withers, the flower fades" only once, and does not have "when the breath of the LORD blows on it. Surely the people are grass."
n.10: Or "will rise up and stand".
n.11: Or "Zion, you who bring good news". The messenger is feminine: either a woman who brings the news, or Zion herself sent to the towns of Judah. Hebrew *mevasseret*, from *basar*, "bring good news" (52:7; 61:1), translated in the Septuagint with the Greek verb from which the New Testament word for "good news" comes. Also in the next line.
n.12: The *reward* and *recompense* are the people he has won back, whom he brings with him (62:11; compare Revelation 22:12).
n.13: Literally "in his bosom", the fold of the garment over the chest.
n.14: Hebrew *zeret*, the width of a spread hand, from thumb to little finger. A *measure* is literally "a third", perhaps a third of an ephah.
n.15: Or "mind". Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, wind, breath".
n.16: Romans 11:34 and 1 Corinthians 2:16 quote this verse from the Septuagint: "Who has known the mind of the Lord? Who has been his counselor?" In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, YHWH ("the LORD").
n.17: The islands and coasts of the Mediterranean (11:11), and in these chapters the most distant lands.
n.18: Hebrew *tohu*, the word for the "formless" earth in Genesis 1:2. Also in verse 23.
n.19: Hebrew *El*, "God".
n.20: Hebrew *ha-mesukkan terumah*, of uncertain meaning. Perhaps "the one who is impoverished in offering". Some scholars connect *mesukkan* with an Akkadian word for a kind of hard wood, *musukkannu*: "As an offering, he chooses *musukkannu*, wood that will not rot."
n.21: Literally "Have you not understood the foundations of the earth?" Or "since the foundations of the earth".
n.22: Hebrew *doq*, "fine cloth, gauze", found only here.
n.23: The stars, pictured as an army (34:4). Hebrew *tseva*, as in the title *YHWH tseva'ot*, "the LORD of Armies".
n.24: Literally "and from my God my right passes away".
n.25: Or "They will grow new feathers like eagles" (compare Psalm 103:5). *Eagle* is Hebrew *nesher*, which may also mean the griffon vulture.

v: Be silent before me, you coastlands![^1] Let the peoples renew their strength! Let them come near and then speak; let us come together for judgment.[^2]
הַחֲרִ֤ישׁוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֔ים וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ יִגְּשׁוּ֙ אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ יַחְדָּ֖ו לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט נִקְרָֽבָה׃
Who has stirred up one from the east, whom victory meets at every step?[^3] He hands nations over to him and makes him trample kings.[^4] His sword makes them like dust, his bow like driven straw.
מִ֤י הֵעִיר֙ מִמִּזְרָ֔ח צֶ֖דֶק יִקְרָאֵ֣הוּ לְרַגְל֑וֹ יִתֵּ֨ן לְפָנָ֤יו גּוֹיִם֙ וּמְלָכִ֣ים יַ֔רְדְּ יִתֵּ֤ן כֶּֽעָפָר֙ חַרְבּ֔וֹ כְּקַ֥שׁ נִדָּ֖ף קַשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
He pursues them and passes on unharmed, by a path his feet have never traveled.[^5]
יִרְדְּפֵ֖ם יַעֲב֣וֹר שָׁל֑וֹם אֹ֥רַח בְּרַגְלָ֖יו לֹ֥א יָבֽוֹא׃
Who has done this and carried it out, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD,[^6] am the first, and with the last I am he.[^7]
מִֽי־פָעַ֣ל וְעָשָׂ֔ה קֹרֵ֥א הַדֹּר֖וֹת מֵרֹ֑אשׁ אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ רִאשׁ֔וֹן וְאֶת־אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים אֲנִי־הֽוּא׃
The coastlands have seen it and are afraid; the ends of the earth tremble. They have drawn near and come.
רָא֤וּ אִיִּים֙ וְיִירָ֔אוּ קְצ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ קָרְב֖וּ וַיֶּאֱתָיֽוּן׃
Each one helps his neighbor and says to his brother, "Be strong!"
אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֖הוּ יַעְזֹ֑רוּ וּלְאָחִ֖יו יֹאמַ֥ר חֲזָֽק׃

The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and the one who smooths with the hammer encourages the one who strikes the anvil. He says of the soldering, "It is good." He fastens the idol with nails so that it will not topple.[^8]
וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק חָרָשׁ֙ אֶת־צֹרֵ֔ף מַחֲלִ֥יק פַּטִּ֖ישׁ אֶת־ה֣וֹלֶם פָּ֑עַם אֹמֵ֤ר לַדֶּ֙בֶק֙ ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַיְחַזְּקֵ֥הוּ בְמַסְמְרִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט׃ ס
But you, Israel, my servant,[^9] Jacob, whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham my friend,[^10]
וְאַתָּה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדִּ֔י יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ זֶ֖רַע אַבְרָהָ֥ם אֹהֲבִֽי׃
you whom I took hold of from the ends of the earth and called from its farthest corners, and to whom I said, "You are my servant; I have chosen you and have not rejected you":
אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶחֱזַקְתִּ֙יךָ֙ מִקְצ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵאֲצִילֶ֖יהָ קְרָאתִ֑יךָ וָאֹ֤מַר לְךָ֙ עַבְדִּי־אַ֔תָּה בְּחַרְתִּ֖יךָ וְלֹ֥א מְאַסְתִּֽיךָ׃
Do not be afraid, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will help you; I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.[^11]
אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י עִמְּךָ־אָ֔נִי אַל־תִּשְׁתָּ֖ע כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אִמַּצְתִּ֙יךָ֙ אַף־עֲזַרְתִּ֔יךָ אַף־תְּמַכְתִּ֖יךָ בִּימִ֥ין צִדְקִֽי׃
Look, all who rage against you will be put to shame and disgraced. Those who contend with you will be as nothing and will perish.
הֵ֤ן יֵבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ וְיִכָּ֣לְמ֔וּ כֹּ֖ל הַנֶּחֱרִ֣ים בָּ֑ךְ יִֽהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וְיֹאבְד֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י רִיבֶֽךָ׃
You will look for those who quarrel with you, but you will not find them. Those who make war against you will be as nothing, nothing at all.
תְּבַקְשֵׁם֙ וְלֹ֣א תִמְצָאֵ֔ם אַנְשֵׁ֖י מַצֻּתֶ֑ךָ יִהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וּכְאֶ֖פֶס אַנְשֵׁ֥י מִלְחַמְתֶּֽךָ׃
For I, the LORD your God, take hold of your right hand and say to you, "Do not be afraid; I will help you."
כִּ֗י אֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מַחֲזִ֣יק יְמִינֶ֑ךָ הָאֹמֵ֥ר לְךָ֛ אַל־תִּירָ֖א אֲנִ֥י עֲזַרְתִּֽיךָ׃ ס
Do not be afraid, you worm Jacob, you little band of Israel![^12] I will help you, declares the LORD; your Redeemer[^13] is the Holy One of Israel.
אַל־תִּֽירְאִי֙ תּוֹלַ֣עַת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב מְתֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֤י עֲזַרְתִּיךְ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Look, I will make you into a threshing sledge,[^14] new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and make the hills like chaff.
הִנֵּ֣ה שַׂמְתִּ֗יךְ לְמוֹרַג֙ חָר֣וּץ חָדָ֔שׁ בַּ֖עַל פִּֽיפִיּ֑וֹת תָּד֤וּשׁ הָרִים֙ וְתָדֹ֔ק וּגְבָע֖וֹת כַּמֹּ֥ץ תָּשִֽׂים׃
You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the storm will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
תִּזְרֵם֙ וְר֣וּחַ תִּשָּׂאֵ֔ם וּסְעָרָ֖ה תָּפִ֣יץ אוֹתָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל בַּֽיהוָ֔ה בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּתְהַלָּֽל׃ פ
The poor and needy look for water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
הָעֲנִיִּ֨ים וְהָאֶבְיוֹנִ֜ים מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים מַ֙יִם֙ וָאַ֔יִן לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם בַּצָּמָ֣א נָשָׁ֑תָּה אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶעֱנֵ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א אֶעֶזְבֵֽם׃
I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the wilderness into pools of water, and the dry land into springs of water.
אֶפְתַּ֤ח עַל־שְׁפָיִים֙ נְהָר֔וֹת וּבְת֥וֹךְ בְּקָע֖וֹת מַעְיָנ֑וֹת אָשִׂ֤ים מִדְבָּר֙ לַאֲגַם־מַ֔יִם וְאֶ֥רֶץ צִיָּ֖ה לְמוֹצָ֥אֵי מָֽיִם׃
I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle and the olive. I will set in the desert the juniper, the plane tree and the pine together,[^15]
אֶתֵּ֤ן בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֶ֣רֶז שִׁטָּ֔ה וַהֲדַ֖ס וְעֵ֣ץ שָׁ֑מֶן אָשִׂ֣ים בָּעֲרָבָ֗ה בְּר֛וֹשׁ תִּדְהָ֥ר וּתְאַשּׁ֖וּר יַחְדָּֽו׃
so that people may see and know, may consider and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
לְמַ֧עַן יִרְא֣וּ וְיֵדְע֗וּ וְיָשִׂ֤ימוּ וְיַשְׂכִּ֙ילוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כִּ֥י יַד־יְהוָ֖ה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּ֑את וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּרָאָֽהּ׃ פ
Present your case, says the LORD; bring forward your arguments,[^16] says the King of Jacob.
קָרְב֥וּ רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הַגִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ עֲצֻמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם יֹאמַ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

Let them come forward and tell us what is going to happen.[^17] Tell us the former things, what they were, so that we may consider them and know how they turned out. Or announce to us the things to come.
יַגִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקְרֶ֑ינָה הָרִאשֹׁנ֣וֹת ׀ מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה הַגִּ֜ידוּ וְנָשִׂ֤ימָה לִבֵּ֙נוּ֙ וְנֵדְעָ֣ה אַחֲרִיתָ֔ן א֥וֹ הַבָּא֖וֹת הַשְׁמִיעֻֽנוּ׃
Tell us what is coming hereafter, so that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do something, good or bad, so that we may be dismayed and see it together.[^18]
הַגִּ֙ידוּ֙ הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת לְאָח֔וֹר וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם אַף־תֵּיטִ֣יבוּ וְתָרֵ֔עוּ וְנִשְׁתָּ֖עָה *ונרא **וְנִרְאֶ֥ה יַחְדָּֽו׃
Look, you are less than nothing, and your work is less than nothing.[^19] Whoever chooses you is detestable.
הֵן־אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן וּפָעָלְכֶ֖ם מֵאָ֑פַע תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה יִבְחַ֥ר בָּכֶֽם׃
I stirred up one from the north, and he has come, one from the rising of the sun who calls on my name.[^20] He will tread on rulers[^21] as on mortar, as a potter treads clay.
הַעִיר֤וֹתִי מִצָּפוֹן֙ וַיַּ֔את מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ יִקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֑י וְיָבֹ֤א סְגָנִים֙ כְּמוֹ־חֹ֔מֶר וּכְמ֥וֹ יוֹצֵ֖ר יִרְמָס־טִֽיט׃
Who announced this from the beginning, so that we could know, and beforehand, so that we could say, "He is right"? No one announced it; no one proclaimed it; no one heard any words from you.
מִֽי־הִגִּ֤יד מֵרֹאשׁ֙ וְנֵדָ֔עָה וּמִלְּפָנִ֖ים וְנֹאמַ֣ר צַדִּ֑יק אַ֣ף אֵין־מַגִּ֗יד אַ֚ף אֵ֣ין מַשְׁמִ֔יעַ אַ֥ף אֵין־שֹׁמֵ֖עַ אִמְרֵיכֶֽם׃
I was the first to say to Zion, "Look, here they are!" and I give Jerusalem a messenger of good news.[^22]
רִאשׁ֥וֹן לְצִיּ֖וֹן הִנֵּ֣ה הִנָּ֑ם וְלִירוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם מְבַשֵּׂ֥ר אֶתֵּֽן׃
But I look, and there is no one; among these there is no counselor who can give an answer when I ask them.
וְאֵ֙רֶא֙ וְאֵ֣ין אִ֔ישׁ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֵ֣ין יוֹעֵ֑ץ וְאֶשְׁאָלֵ֖ם וְיָשִׁ֥יבוּ דָבָֽר׃
Look, all of them are a delusion;[^23] their works are nothing; their cast images are wind and emptiness.[^24]
הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם אָ֥וֶן אֶ֖פֶס מַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם ר֥וּחַ וָתֹ֖הוּ נִסְכֵּיהֶֽם׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *iyyim*, the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean (11:11), and in these chapters the most distant lands. Also in verse 5.
n.2: The nations and their gods are summoned to a court of law. The trial scene returns in verses 21–29.
n.3: Literally "whom righteousness calls to his foot". Hebrew *tsedeq*, "righteousness", here the right that wins out, God's saving purpose carried out through the conqueror. Or "whom he calls in righteousness to his service". The conqueror from the east (and the north, verse 25) is Cyrus of Persia, named in 44:28 and 45:1.
n.4: Or "subdues kings before him". The meaning of the Hebrew verb *yard* is uncertain.
n.5: Literally "a path with his feet he does not come", perhaps "so swiftly that his feet hardly touch the path".
n.6: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.7: Hebrew *ani hu*, "I am he", a solemn self-declaration of God found often in these chapters (43:10, 13; 46:4; 48:12; compare Deuteronomy 32:39). The Septuagint translates it here as *ego eimi*, "I am" (compare John 8:24, 28).
n.8: Literally "fastens it". Verses 6–7 describe the makers of idols, who encourage one another as the nations draw near.
n.9: Hebrew *eved*, "servant". In chapters 41–53 the LORD often calls Israel "my servant" (44:1–2, 21; 45:4; 48:20). On the servant passages, see 42:1.
n.10: Literally "who loved me". 2 Chronicles 20:7 and James 2:23 also call Abraham God's friend.
n.11: Literally "the right hand of my righteousness". Or "my victorious right hand".
n.12: Literally "you men of Israel". Hebrew *metim*, a word used of a small number of people (Deuteronomy 4:27). *You* is feminine in the Hebrew, matching *worm*.
n.13: Hebrew *go'el*, a close relative with the duty to protect a family member in need: to buy back land a relative had sold, to free a relative sold into slavery, and to avenge a killing (Leviticus 25:25, 47–49; Numbers 35:19; Ruth 2:20). In chapters 41–63 it is a title of God, who acts as Israel's next of kin.
n.14: A heavy board with sharp stones or iron set into its underside, dragged over grain to separate it from the husks.
n.15: The identification of several of these trees is uncertain. *Olive* is literally "tree of oil", perhaps the wild olive or another tree that gives oil or resin; *juniper* (Hebrew *berosh*) may be the cypress (14:8); *plane tree* (*tidhar*) and *pine* (*te'ashur*) may be the elm and the cypress or box tree. The three trees are named together again in 60:13.
n.16: Literally "your strong things".
n.17: The LORD challenges the gods of the nations to foretell the future.
n.18: The Hebrew text is written with letters that may be read "and be afraid", but is read "and see".
n.19: Hebrew *me'afa*, found only here, probably a form of *me'efes*, "less than nothing" (40:17).
n.20: Or "who will be called by my name".
n.21: Literally "He will come upon rulers". Hebrew *seganim*, "governors, officials", a word borrowed from Akkadian.
n.22: The Hebrew of this verse is very short and difficult. Literally "First to Zion: Look, look at them! And to Jerusalem I give a bringer of good news." *Messenger of good news* is the word used in 40:9.

v: Here is my servant,[^1] whom I uphold, my chosen one, in whom I delight.[^2] I have put my Spirit[^3] on him; he will bring justice[^4] to the nations.
הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ אֶתְמָךְ־בּ֔וֹ בְּחִירִ֖י רָצְתָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י נָתַ֤תִּי רוּחִי֙ עָלָ֔יו מִשְׁפָּ֖ט לַגּוֹיִ֥ם יוֹצִֽיא׃
He will not cry out or raise his voice, or make his voice heard in the street.
לֹ֥א יִצְעַ֖ק וְלֹ֣א יִשָּׂ֑א וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁמִ֥יעַ בַּח֖וּץ קוֹלֽוֹ׃
A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out. He will faithfully bring justice.[^5]
קָנֶ֤ה רָצוּץ֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁבּ֔וֹר וּפִשְׁתָּ֥ה כֵהָ֖ה לֹ֣א יְכַבֶּ֑נָּה לֶאֱמֶ֖ת יוֹצִ֥יא מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
He will not grow dim or be bruised[^6] until he has established justice on the earth, and the coastlands[^7] wait for his instruction.[^8]
לֹ֤א יִכְהֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א יָר֔וּץ עַד־יָשִׂ֥ים בָּאָ֖רֶץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּלְתוֹרָת֖וֹ אִיִּ֥ים יְיַחֵֽילוּ׃ פ

This is what God, the LORD,[^9] says, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and all that comes from it, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk on it:
כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל ׀ יְהוָ֗ה בּוֹרֵ֤א הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְנ֣וֹטֵיהֶ֔ם רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ וְצֶאֱצָאֶ֑יהָ נֹתֵ֤ן נְשָׁמָה֙ לָעָ֣ם עָלֶ֔יהָ וְר֖וּחַ לַהֹלְכִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃
I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness;[^10] I will take hold of your hand. I will keep you[^11] and make you a covenant for the people,[^12] a light for the nations,
אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה קְרָאתִ֥יךָֽ בְצֶ֖דֶק וְאַחְזֵ֣ק בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְאֶצָּרְךָ֗ וְאֶתֶּנְךָ֛ לִבְרִ֥ית עָ֖ם לְא֥וֹר גּוֹיִֽם׃
to open eyes that are blind, to bring prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
לִפְקֹ֖חַ עֵינַ֣יִם עִוְר֑וֹת לְהוֹצִ֤יא מִמַּסְגֵּר֙ אַסִּ֔יר מִבֵּ֥ית כֶּ֖לֶא יֹ֥שְׁבֵי חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
I am the LORD; that is my name. I will not give my glory to another, or my praise to idols.
אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא שְׁמִ֑י וּכְבוֹדִי֙ לְאַחֵ֣ר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֔ן וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י לַפְּסִילִֽים׃
Look, the former things have come to pass, and new things I now declare. Before they spring up, I tell you of them.
הָרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת הִנֵּה־בָ֑אוּ וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד בְּטֶ֥רֶם תִּצְמַ֖חְנָה אַשְׁמִ֥יע אֶתְכֶֽם׃ פ
Sing to the LORD a new song,[^13] his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, you coastlands and those who live in them.
שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ מִקְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ יוֹרְדֵ֤י הַיָּם֙ וּמְלֹא֔וֹ אִיִּ֖ים וְיֹשְׁבֵיהֶֽם׃
Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices, the villages where Kedar[^14] lives. Let the people of Sela[^15] sing for joy; let them shout from the tops of the mountains.
יִשְׂא֤וּ מִדְבָּר֙ וְעָרָ֔יו חֲצֵרִ֖ים תֵּשֵׁ֣ב קֵדָ֑ר יָרֹ֙נּוּ֙ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי סֶ֔לַע מֵרֹ֥אשׁ הָרִ֖ים יִצְוָֽחוּ׃
Let them give glory to the LORD and declare his praise in the coastlands.
יָשִׂ֥ימוּ לַֽיהוָ֖ה כָּב֑וֹד וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ׃
The LORD goes out like a warrior; like a man of war he stirs up his zeal. He shouts, yes, he roars; he shows his might against his enemies.
יְהוָה֙ כַּגִּבּ֣וֹר יֵצֵ֔א כְּאִ֥ישׁ מִלְחָמ֖וֹת יָעִ֣יר קִנְאָ֑ה יָרִ֙יעַ֙ אַף־יַצְרִ֔יחַ עַל־אֹיְבָ֖יו יִתְגַּבָּֽר׃ ס
For a long time I have kept silent; I have been still and held myself back. Now, like a woman in labor, I will cry out; I will gasp and pant.
הֶחֱשֵׁ֙יתִי֙ מֵֽעוֹלָ֔ם אַחֲרִ֖ישׁ אֶתְאַפָּ֑ק כַּיּוֹלֵדָ֣ה אֶפְעֶ֔ה אֶשֹּׁ֥ם וְאֶשְׁאַ֖ף יָֽחַד׃
I will lay waste mountains and hills and dry up all their plants. I will turn rivers into dry land[^16] and dry up the pools.
אַחֲרִ֤יב הָרִים֙ וּגְבָע֔וֹת וְכָל־עֶשְׂבָּ֖ם אוֹבִ֑ישׁ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י נְהָרוֹת֙ לֽ͏ָאִיִּ֔ים וַאֲגַמִּ֖ים אוֹבִֽישׁ׃

I will lead the blind by a way they do not know; I will guide them on paths they have not known. I will turn the darkness before them into light, and the rough places into level ground. These are the things I will do,[^17] and I will not abandon them.

וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים בְּדֶ֙רֶךְ֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ בִּנְתִיב֥וֹת לֹֽא־יָדְע֖וּ אַדְרִיכֵ֑ם אָשִׂים֩ מַחְשָׁ֨ךְ לִפְנֵיהֶ֜ם לָא֗וֹר וּמַֽעֲקַשִּׁים֙ לְמִישׁ֔וֹר אֵ֚לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֔ים עֲשִׂיתִ֖ם וְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתִּֽים׃
They will be turned back and utterly put to shame, those who trust in idols, who say to cast images, "You are our gods."
נָסֹ֤גוּ אָחוֹר֙ יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ בֹ֔שֶׁת הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בַּפָּ֑סֶל הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לְמַסֵּכָ֖ה אַתֶּ֥ם אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ ס
Listen, you deaf! Look, you blind, so that you may see!
הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים שְׁמָ֑עוּ וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים הַבִּ֥יטוּ לִרְאֽוֹת׃
Who is blind but my servant, or deaf like my messenger whom I send? Who is blind like the one at peace with me,[^18] blind like the servant of the LORD?
מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּ֣י אִם־עַבְדִּ֔י וְחֵרֵ֖שׁ כְּמַלְאָכִ֣י אֶשְׁלָ֑ח מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּמְשֻׁלָּ֔ם וְעִוֵּ֖ר כְּעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה׃
You see many things,[^19] but you do not take note of them; his ears are open, but he does not hear.
*ראית **רָא֥וֹת רַבּ֖וֹת וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמֹ֑ר פָּק֥וֹחַ אָזְנַ֖יִם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמָֽע׃
The LORD was pleased, for the sake of his righteousness, to make his instruction great and glorious.
יְהוָ֥ה חָפֵ֖ץ לְמַ֣עַן צִדְק֑וֹ יַגְדִּ֥יל תּוֹרָ֖ה וְיַאְדִּֽיר׃
But this is a people plundered and looted, all of them trapped in holes[^20] and hidden away in prisons. They have become plunder with no one to rescue them, loot with no one to say, "Give it back!"
וְהוּא֮ עַם־בָּז֣וּז וְשָׁסוּי֒ הָפֵ֤חַ בַּֽחוּרִים֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם וּבְבָתֵּ֥י כְלָאִ֖ים הָחְבָּ֑אוּ הָי֤וּ לָבַז֙ וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּ֔יל מְשִׁסָּ֖ה וְאֵין־אֹמֵ֥ר הָשַֽׁב׃
Who among you will listen to this, pay attention and hear it for the time to come?
מִ֥י בָכֶ֖ם יַאֲזִ֣ין זֹ֑את יַקְשִׁ֥ב וְיִשְׁמַ֖ע לְאָחֽוֹר׃
Who handed Jacob over to be looted, and Israel to plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They would not walk in his ways, and they did not obey his instruction.
מִֽי־נָתַ֨ן *למשוסה **לִמְשִׁסָּ֧ה יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים הֲל֣וֹא יְהוָ֑ה ז֚וּ חָטָ֣אנוּ ל֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־אָב֤וּ בִדְרָכָיו֙ הָל֔וֹךְ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּתוֹרָתֽוֹ׃
So he poured out on him his burning anger and the fury of battle. It set him on fire all around, but he did not understand; it burned him, but he did not take it to heart.
וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֤ךְ עָלָיו֙ חֵמָ֣ה אַפּ֔וֹ וֶעֱז֖וּז מִלְחָמָ֑ה וַתְּלַהֲטֵ֤הוּ מִסָּבִיב֙ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֔ע וַתִּבְעַר־בּ֖וֹ וְלֹא־יָשִׂ֥ים עַל־לֵֽב׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *avdi*, "my servant". Verses 1–9 are the first of four passages about the servant of the LORD that are often called the "Servant Songs" (42:1–9; 49:1–13; 50:4–11; 52:13–53:12; scholars count their limits differently). In the chapters around them the servant is Israel (41:8–9; 44:1–2), and 49:3 calls him "Israel", yet he also has a task toward Israel (49:5–6). He has been identified with the people of Israel, a faithful part of the people, the prophet himself, a king, or a figure still to come. The Septuagint reads "Jacob my servant … Israel my chosen one". The Aramaic Targum reads "my servant, the anointed one (Messiah)". In the New Testament the servant passages are applied to Jesus: Matthew 12:18–21 quotes verses 1–4, and the words from heaven at Jesus' baptism echo verse 1 (Mark 1:11).
n.2: Literally "in whom my *nephesh* delights".
n.3: Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, wind, breath".
n.4: Hebrew *mishpat*, "justice, judgment", the right order that God decrees. Also in verses 3–4.
n.5: Or "In faithfulness he will bring out justice".
n.6: A play on words: *lo yikheh*, "he will not grow dim", and *lo yaruts*, "he will not be bruised", echo the "smoldering" (*kehah*) wick and the "bruised" (*ratsuts*) reed of verse 3.
n.7: Hebrew *iyyim*, the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean (11:11), and in these chapters the most distant lands. Also in verses 10 and 12.
n.8: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching, law". Also in verses 21 and 24. Matthew 12:21 quotes the Septuagint: "and in his name the nations will hope".
n.9: Hebrew *ha-el YHWH*, "the God, the LORD". *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.10: Or "for a righteous purpose". Hebrew *tsedeq*.
n.11: Or "I will form you". The Hebrew form can come from either verb.
n.12: Hebrew *berit am*, "a covenant of people", perhaps "a covenant for the people of Israel" or "a covenant for humankind". The phrase is repeated in 49:8. Simeon's words in Luke 2:32, "a light for revelation to the nations", echo this verse and 49:6.
n.13: Compare Psalms 96:1 and 98:1.
n.14: A tribe of the Arabian desert (21:16–17).
n.15: Hebrew *sela*, "rock", perhaps the Edomite city of Sela (16:1), or "those who live among the rocks".
n.16: Hebrew *iyyim*, elsewhere "coastlands" or "islands" (verse 10). Here it seems to mean dry land.
n.17: Literally "I have done them". The future is spoken of as if it were already done.
n.18: Hebrew *meshullam*, perhaps "the one in a covenant of peace with me", "the one made complete" or "the one paid for". The meaning is uncertain.
n.19: The Hebrew text is written "You have seen many things" but read "Seeing many things".
n.20: Hebrew *ba-churim*. The same consonants can be read *bachurim*, "young men": "all their young men are trapped".

v: But now, this is what the LORD[^1] says, he who created you, Jacob, he who formed you, Israel: Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you;[^2] I have called you by name; you are mine.
וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י גְאַלְתִּ֔יךָ קָרָ֥אתִי בְשִׁמְךָ֖ לִי־אָֽתָּה׃
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through fire, you will not be burned, and the flame will not consume you.
כִּֽי־תַעֲבֹ֤ר בַּמַּ֙יִם֙ אִתְּךָ־אָ֔נִי וּבַנְּהָר֖וֹת לֹ֣א יִשְׁטְפ֑וּךָ כִּֽי־תֵלֵ֤ךְ בְּמוֹ־אֵשׁ֙ לֹ֣א תִכָּוֶ֔ה וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר־בָּֽךְ׃
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I give Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba[^3] in exchange for you.
כִּ֗י אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ נָתַ֤תִּי כָפְרְךָ֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם כּ֥וּשׁ וּסְבָ֖א תַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃
Because you are precious in my eyes, and honored, and I love you, I give people in exchange for you, and nations in exchange for your life.
מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָקַ֧רְתָּ בְעֵינַ֛י נִכְבַּ֖דְתָּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֲהַבְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֶתֵּ֤ן אָדָם֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יךָ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים תַּ֥חַת נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
אַל־תִּירָ֖א כִּ֣י אִתְּךָ־אָ֑נִי מִמִּזְרָח֙ אָבִ֣יא זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֖ב אֲקַבְּצֶֽךָּ׃
I will say to the north, "Give them up!" and to the south,[^4] "Do not hold them back! Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the end of the earth,
אֹמַ֤ר לַצָּפוֹן֙ תֵּ֔נִי וּלְתֵימָ֖ן אַל־תִּכְלָ֑אִי הָבִ֤יאִי בָנַי֙ מֵרָח֔וֹק וּבְנוֹתַ֖י מִקְצֵ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃
everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed and made."
כֹּ֚ל הַנִּקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֔י וְלִכְבוֹדִ֖י בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף־עֲשִׂיתִֽיו׃
Bring out the people who are blind, though they have eyes, who are deaf, though they have ears.
הוֹצִ֥יא עַם־עִוֵּ֖ר וְעֵינַ֣יִם יֵ֑שׁ וְחֵרְשִׁ֖ים וְאָזְנַ֥יִם לָֽמוֹ׃

Let all the nations gather together, and let the peoples assemble. Who among them can declare this and tell us the former things? Let them bring their witnesses to prove they are right, so that others may hear and say, "It is true."
כָּֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו וְיֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ לְאֻמִּ֔ים מִ֤י בָהֶם֙ יַגִּ֣יד זֹ֔את וְרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת יַשְׁמִיעֻ֑נוּ יִתְּנ֤וּ עֵֽדֵיהֶם֙ וְיִצְדָּ֔קוּ וְיִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְיֹאמְר֥וּ אֱמֶֽת׃

You are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen,[^5] so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he.[^6] Before me no god was formed, and after me there will be none.
אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְעַבְדִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחָ֑רְתִּי לְמַ֣עַן תֵּ֠דְעוּ וְתַאֲמִ֨ינוּ לִ֤י וְתָבִ֙ינוּ֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא לְפָנַי֙ לֹא־נ֣וֹצַר אֵ֔ל וְאַחֲרַ֖י לֹ֥א יִהְיֶֽה׃ ס
I, I am the LORD, and apart from me there is no savior.
אָנֹכִ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין מִבַּלְעָדַ֖י מוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
I declared and saved and proclaimed, and there was no foreign god among you. You are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and I am God.
אָנֹכִ֞י הִגַּ֤דְתִּי וְהוֹשַׁ֙עְתִּי֙ וְהִשְׁמַ֔עְתִּי וְאֵ֥ין בָּכֶ֖ם זָ֑ר וְאַתֶּ֥ם עֵדַ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽאֲנִי־אֵֽל׃
From this day on[^7] I am he. No one can rescue from my hand. I act, and who can turn it back?
גַּם־מִיּוֹם֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא וְאֵ֥ין מִיָּדִ֖י מַצִּ֑יל אֶפְעַ֖ל וּמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃ ס

This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer,[^8] the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I am sending to Babylon. I will bring them all down as fugitives,[^9] and the Chaldeans in the ships they shouted over.[^10]
כֹּֽה־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְמַעַנְכֶ֞ם שִׁלַּ֣חְתִּי בָבֶ֗לָה וְהוֹרַדְתִּ֤י בָֽרִיחִים֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם וְכַשְׂדִּ֖ים בָּאֳנִיּ֥וֹת רִנָּתָֽם׃
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.
אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה קְדֽוֹשְׁכֶ֑ם בּוֹרֵ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מַלְכְּכֶֽם׃ ס
This is what the LORD says, who makes a way through the sea, a path through the mighty waters,
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ וּבְמַ֥יִם עַזִּ֖ים נְתִיבָֽה׃
who brings out chariot and horse, army and warrior together. They lie down, never to rise again; they are snuffed out, quenched like a wick.[^11]
הַמּוֹצִ֥יא רֶֽכֶב־וָס֖וּס חַ֣יִל וְעִזּ֑וּז יַחְדָּ֤ו יִשְׁכְּבוּ֙ בַּל־יָק֔וּמוּ דָּעֲכ֖וּ כַּפִּשְׁתָּ֥ה כָבֽוּ׃
Do not remember the former things, or consider the things of old.
אַֽל־תִּזְכְּר֖וּ רִֽאשֹׁנ֑וֹת וְקַדְמֹנִיּ֖וֹת אַל־תִּתְבֹּנָֽנוּ׃
Look, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the wasteland.
הִנְנִ֨י עֹשֶׂ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ עַתָּ֣ה תִצְמָ֔ח הֲל֖וֹא תֵּֽדָע֑וּהָ אַ֣ף אָשִׂ֤ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ דֶּ֔רֶךְ בִּֽישִׁמ֖וֹן נְהָרֽוֹת׃
The wild animals will honor me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I give water in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
תְּכַבְּדֵ֙נִי֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה תַּנִּ֖ים וּבְנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה כִּֽי־נָתַ֨תִּי בַמִּדְבָּ֜ר מַ֗יִם נְהָרוֹת֙ בִּֽישִׁימֹ֔ן לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת עַמִּ֥י בְחִירִֽי׃
the people I formed for myself, so that they may declare my praise.
עַם־זוּ֙ יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י תְּהִלָּתִ֖י יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃ ס
Yet you have not called on me, Jacob; you have grown weary of me, Israel.
וְלֹא־אֹתִ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב כִּֽי־יָגַ֥עְתָּ בִּ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
You have not brought me sheep for your burnt offerings, or honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with grain offerings,[^12] or wearied you with demands for frankincense.
לֹֽא־הֵבֵ֤יאתָ לִּי֙ שֵׂ֣ה עֹלֹתֶ֔יךָ וּזְבָחֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א כִבַּדְתָּ֑נִי לֹ֤א הֶעֱבַדְתִּ֙יךָ֙ בְּמִנְחָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א הוֹגַעְתִּ֖יךָ בִּלְבוֹנָֽה׃
You have not bought me sweet cane[^13] with silver, or filled me with the fat of your sacrifices. Instead you have burdened me with your sins; you have wearied me with your wrongdoing.[^14]
לֹא־קָנִ֨יתָ לִּ֤י בַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ קָנֶ֔ה וְחֵ֥לֶב זְבָחֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א הִרְוִיתָ֑נִי אַ֗ךְ הֶעֱבַדְתַּ֙נִי֙ בְּחַטֹּאותֶ֔יךָ הוֹגַעְתַּ֖נִי בַּעֲוֺנֹתֶֽיךָ׃ ס
I, I am he who wipes out your rebellious acts for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
אָנֹכִ֨י אָנֹכִ֥י ה֛וּא מֹחֶ֥ה פְשָׁעֶ֖יךָ לְמַעֲנִ֑י וְחַטֹּאתֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א אֶזְכֹּֽר׃
Remind me; let us go to court together. State your case, so that you may be proved right.
הַזְכִּירֵ֕נִי נִשָּׁפְטָ֖ה יָ֑חַד סַפֵּ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה לְמַ֥עַן תִּצְדָּֽק׃
Your first ancestor[^15] sinned, and your spokesmen[^16] rebelled against me.
אָבִ֥יךָ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן חָטָ֑א וּמְלִיצֶ֖יךָ פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃
So I profaned the princes of the sanctuary;[^17] I handed Jacob over to destruction[^18] and Israel to scorn.
וַאֲחַלֵּ֖ל שָׂ֣רֵי קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לַחֵ֙רֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְגִדּוּפִֽים׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *ga'al*, the verb of the *go'el*, the next of kin who buys back or rescues a family member (41:14).
n.3: *Cush* is the region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia); *Seba* was probably also in Africa (Genesis 10:7; Psalm 72:10).
n.4: Literally "Teman", the south. The commands to the north and the south are in the feminine form, as if to women holding captives.
n.5: Or "You are my witnesses, declares the LORD, my servant whom I have chosen". The servant is Israel, as in 41:8 and 44:1.
n.6: Hebrew *ani hu* (41:4). Also in verse 13. The Septuagint translates "that I am" (*ego eimi*), and John 8:28 and 13:19 echo it.
n.7: Or "From the beginning of days". Literally "Also from the day".
n.8: Hebrew *go'el* (41:14).
n.9: Or "I will break down all the bars", that is, of the city's gates. Hebrew *barichim* can mean "fugitives", and with other vowels "bars". The Hebrew of the verse is difficult.
n.10: Literally "in the ships their shout", perhaps the ships they had once been proud of, or ships in which their shouts of joy turn to cries.
n.11: The destruction of Pharaoh's army at the Red Sea (Exodus 14–15). The same word for *wick* is used in 42:3.
n.12: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute", in Leviticus a grain offering. *Burdened* is literally "made you serve".
n.13: Hebrew *qaneh*, "reed", an aromatic cane used to make the anointing oil (Exodus 30:23, "fragrant cane"). A play on words: *lo qanita … qaneh*, "you have not bought … cane".
n.14: *Burdened me* and *wearied me* are the verbs of verse 23: Israel has not served the LORD, but has made the LORD serve Israel's sins.
n.15: Literally "Your first father", perhaps Jacob (Hosea 12:3–5; 12:2–4 in most English Bibles), or Abraham.
n.16: Hebrew *melitsim*, "interpreters, go-betweens", perhaps the priests and prophets.
n.17: Or "the holy princes", perhaps the priests. The Hebrew verbs in this verse can also be read as future: "So I will profane … I will hand Jacob over".
n.18: Hebrew *cherem*, "devotion to destruction" (34:2).

v: But now listen, Jacob my servant, Israel whom I have chosen.
וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃
This is what the LORD[^1] says, who made you, who formed you from the womb and will help you: Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, Jeshurun[^2] whom I have chosen.
כֹּה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן יַעְזְרֶ֑ךָּ אַל־תִּירָא֙ עַבְדִּ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וִישֻׁר֖וּן בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃
For I will pour water on the thirsty land and streams on the dry ground. I will pour out my Spirit[^3] on your offspring and my blessing on your descendants.
כִּ֤י אֶצָּק־מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־צָמֵ֔א וְנֹזְלִ֖ים עַל־יַבָּשָׁ֑ה אֶצֹּ֤ק רוּחִי֙ עַל־זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּבִרְכָתִ֖י עַל־צֶאֱצָאֶֽיךָ׃
They will spring up among the grass,[^4] like willows by streams of water.
וְצָמְח֖וּ בְּבֵ֣ין חָצִ֑יר כַּעֲרָבִ֖ים עַל־יִבְלֵי־מָֽיִם׃
One will say, "I belong to the LORD"; another will call himself by the name of Jacob; another will write on his hand, "The LORD's,"[^5] and take the name of Israel as his title.
זֶ֤ה יֹאמַר֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אָ֔נִי וְזֶ֖ה יִקְרָ֣א בְשֵֽׁם־יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְזֶ֗ה יִכְתֹּ֤ב יָדוֹ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְשֵׁ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יְכַנֶּֽה׃ פ
This is what the LORD says, the King of Israel and its Redeemer,[^6] the LORD of Armies:[^7] I am the first and I am the last; apart from me there is no God.[^8]
כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְגֹאֲל֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אֲנִ֤י רִאשׁוֹן֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲר֔וֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדַ֖י אֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִֽים׃
Who is like me? Let him proclaim it; let him declare it and set it out before me, since I established my ancient people.[^9] Let them declare what is coming, and what is going to happen.
וּמִֽי־כָמ֣וֹנִי יִקְרָ֗א וְיַגִּידֶ֤הָ וְיַעְרְכֶ֙הָ֙ לִ֔י מִשּׂוּמִ֖י עַם־עוֹלָ֑ם וְאֹתִיּ֛וֹת וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֖אנָה יַגִּ֥ידוּ לָֽמוֹ׃
Do not tremble or be afraid. Did I not tell you long ago and declare it? You are my witnesses. Is there any God apart from me? There is no other Rock; I know of none.
אַֽל־תִּפְחֲדוּ֙ וְאַל־תִּרְה֔וּ הֲלֹ֥א מֵאָ֛ז הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י הֲיֵ֤שׁ אֱל֙וֹהַּ֙ מִבַּלְעָדַ֔י וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר בַּל־יָדָֽעְתִּי׃
All who make idols are nothing,[^10] and the things they delight in do no good. Their witnesses[^11] neither see nor know, so they will be put to shame.
יֹֽצְרֵי־פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ וַחֲמוּדֵיהֶ֖ם בַּל־יוֹעִ֑ילוּ וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ[4] בַּל־יִרְא֛וּ וּבַל־יֵדְע֖וּ לְמַ֥עַן יֵבֹֽשׁוּ׃
Who would fashion a god or cast an idol that can do no good?
מִֽי־יָצַ֥ר אֵ֖ל וּפֶ֣סֶל נָסָ֑ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הוֹעִֽיל׃
Look, all who join themselves to it[^12] will be put to shame; the craftsmen are only human. Let them all gather and take their stand; they will be terrified and put to shame together.
הֵ֤ן כָּל־חֲבֵרָיו֙ יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ וְחָרָשִׁ֥ים הֵ֖מָּה מֵֽאָדָ֑ם יִֽתְקַבְּצ֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ יַֽעֲמֹ֔דוּ יִפְחֲד֖וּ יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ יָֽחַד׃

The blacksmith takes a tool and works it over the coals. He shapes the idol with hammers and forges it with his strong arm. He also grows hungry and loses his strength; he drinks no water and grows faint.
חָרַ֤שׁ בַּרְזֶל֙ מַֽעֲצָ֔ד וּפָעַל֙ בַּפֶּחָ֔ם וּבַמַּקָּב֖וֹת יִצְּרֵ֑הוּ וַיִּפְעָלֵ֙הוּ֙ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ כֹּח֔וֹ גַּם־רָעֵב֙ וְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֔חַ לֹא־שָׁ֥תָה מַ֖יִם וַיִּיעָֽף׃

The carpenter stretches out a line and marks it out with a stylus. He shapes it with chisels and marks it with compasses. He makes it in the form of a man, with human beauty, to live in a shrine.[^13]
חָרַ֣שׁ עֵצִים֮ נָ֣טָה קָו֒ יְתָאֲרֵ֣הוּ בַשֶּׂ֔רֶד יַעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ בַּמַּקְצֻע֔וֹת וּבַמְּחוּגָ֖ה יְתָאֳרֵ֑הוּ וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ כְּתַבְנִ֣ית אִ֔ישׁ כְּתִפְאֶ֥רֶת אָדָ֖ם לָשֶׁ֥בֶת בָּֽיִת׃
He cuts down cedars for himself, or takes a cypress[^14] or an oak. He lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. He plants a laurel,[^15] and the rain makes it grow.
לִכְרָת־ל֣וֹ אֲרָזִ֔ים וַיִּקַּ֤ח תִּרְזָה֙ וְאַלּ֔וֹן וַיְאַמֶּץ־ל֖וֹ בַּעֲצֵי־יָ֑עַר נָטַ֥ע אֹ֖רֶן[6] וְגֶ֥שֶׁם יְגַדֵּֽל׃
Then it becomes fuel for people to burn. He takes some of it and warms himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread. He also makes a god and worships it; he makes it an idol and bows down to it.
וְהָיָ֤ה לְאָדָם֙ לְבָעֵ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֵהֶם֙ וַיָּ֔חָם אַף־יַשִּׂ֖יק וְאָ֣פָה לָ֑חֶם אַף־יִפְעַל־אֵל֙ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֔חוּ עָשָׂ֥הוּ פֶ֖סֶל וַיִּסְגָּד־לָֽמוֹ׃
Half of it he burns in the fire. Over that half he eats meat; he roasts a roast and is satisfied. He also warms himself and says, "Ah! I am warm; I have seen the fire!"
חֶצְיוֹ֙ שָׂרַ֣ף בְּמוֹ־אֵ֔שׁ עַל־חֶצְיוֹ֙ בָּשָׂ֣ר יֹאכֵ֔ל יִצְלֶ֥ה צָלִ֖י וְיִשְׂבָּ֑ע אַף־יָחֹם֙ וְיֹאמַ֣ר הֶאָ֔ח חַמּוֹתִ֖י רָאִ֥יתִי אֽוּר׃
And the rest of it he makes into a god, his idol. He bows down to it and worships; he prays to it and says, "Save me, for you are my god!"
וּשְׁאֵ֣רִית֔וֹ לְאֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה לְפִסְל֑וֹ *יסגוד־**יִסְגָּד־ל֤וֹ וְיִשְׁתַּ֙חוּ֙ וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֔יו וְיֹאמַר֙ הַצִּילֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י אֵלִ֖י אָֽתָּה׃
They do not know or understand, for their eyes are plastered over so that they cannot see, and their minds[^16] so that they cannot understand.
לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ינוּ כִּ֣י טַ֤ח מֵֽרְאוֹת֙ עֵֽינֵיהֶ֔ם מֵהַשְׂכִּ֖יל לִבֹּתָֽם׃

No one stops to think;[^17] no one has the knowledge or understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in the fire; I also baked bread on its coals; I roast meat and eat it. Shall I make the rest of it a detestable thing? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?"

וְלֹא־יָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־לִבּ֗וֹ וְלֹ֨א דַ֥עַת וְלֹֽא־תְבוּנָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ חֶצְי֞וֹ שָׂרַ֣פְתִּי בְמוֹ־אֵ֗שׁ וְ֠אַף אָפִ֤יתִי עַל־גֶּחָלָיו֙ לֶ֔חֶם אֶצְלֶ֥ה בָשָׂ֖ר וְאֹכֵ֑ל וְיִתְרוֹ֙ לְתוֹעֵבָ֣ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה לְב֥וּל עֵ֖ץ אֶסְגּֽוֹד׃
He feeds on ashes.[^18] A deceived heart has led him astray, and he cannot save himself[^19] or say, "Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?"
רֹעֶ֣ה אֵ֔פֶר לֵ֥ב הוּתַ֖ל הִטָּ֑הוּ וְלֹֽא־יַצִּ֤יל אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א יֹאמַ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא שֶׁ֖קֶר בִּימִינִֽי׃ ס
Remember these things, Jacob, Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you; you are my servant. Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.[^20]
זְכָר־אֵ֣לֶּה יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י עַבְדִּי־אָ֑תָּה יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד־לִי֙ אַ֔תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א תִנָּשֵֽׁנִי׃
I have wiped out your rebellious acts like a cloud, and your sins like mist. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.
מָחִ֤יתִי כָעָב֙ פְּשָׁעֶ֔יךָ וְכֶעָנָ֖ן חַטֹּאותֶ֑יךָ שׁוּבָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ׃

Sing for joy, you heavens, for the LORD has done it! Shout aloud, you depths of the earth! Break into song, you mountains, you forest and every tree in it! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and he shows his glory in Israel.
רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי־עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה הָרִ֙יעוּ֙ תַּחְתִּיּ֣וֹת אָ֔רֶץ פִּצְח֤וּ הָרִים֙ רִנָּ֔ה יַ֖עַר וְכָל־עֵ֣ץ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־גָאַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִתְפָּאָֽר׃ פ
This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: I am the LORD, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by myself,[^21]
כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן אָנֹכִ֤י יְהוָה֙ עֹ֣שֶׂה כֹּ֔ל נֹטֶ֤ה שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ לְבַדִּ֔י רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ *מי *אתי **מֵאִתִּֽי׃
who frustrates the signs of false prophets[^22] and makes fools of diviners, who turns back the wise and makes their knowledge foolish,
מֵפֵר֙ אֹת֣וֹת בַּדִּ֔ים וְקֹסְמִ֖ים יְהוֹלֵ֑ל מֵשִׁ֧יב חֲכָמִ֛ים אָח֖וֹר וְדַעְתָּ֥ם יְשַׂכֵּֽל׃

who carries out the word of his servant and fulfills the counsel of his messengers, who says of Jerusalem, "She will be inhabited," and of the towns of Judah, "They will be rebuilt, and I will raise up her ruins,"
מֵקִים֙ דְּבַ֣ר עַבְדּ֔וֹ וַעֲצַ֥ת מַלְאָכָ֖יו יַשְׁלִ֑ים הָאֹמֵ֨ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם תּוּשָׁ֗ב וּלְעָרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ינָה וְחָרְבוֹתֶ֖יהָ אֲקוֹמֵֽם׃
who says to the deep, "Be dry! I will dry up your rivers,"[^23]
הָאֹמֵ֥ר לַצּוּלָ֖ה חֳרָ֑בִי וְנַהֲרֹתַ֖יִךְ אוֹבִֽישׁ׃
who says of Cyrus,[^24] "He is my shepherd, and he will carry out all that I desire," saying of Jerusalem, "She will be rebuilt," and of the temple, "Its foundations will be laid."
הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֙וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י וְכָל־חֶפְצִ֖י יַשְׁלִ֑ם וְלֵאמֹ֤ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ה וְהֵיכָ֖ל תִּוָּסֵֽד׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: A poetic name for Israel, perhaps "the upright one" (Deuteronomy 32:15; 33:5, 26).
n.3: Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, wind, breath".
n.4: Literally "in between grass".
n.5: Literally "will write his hand: To the LORD". Or "will write with his hand". The mark would show to whom he belongs, as a slave's or a soldier's mark showed his master.
n.6: Hebrew *go'el* (41:14). Also in verse 24.
n.7: *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.8: Compare 41:4; 48:12. Revelation 1:17; 2:8 and 22:13 echo these words.
n.9: Literally "since I set up a people of long ago". The meaning is uncertain.
n.10: Hebrew *tohu*, "emptiness" (40:17).
n.11: In the Hebrew text, dots are written over the next word (*hemmah*, "they"), a scribal mark of doubt.
n.12: Literally "all its companions", that is, its worshipers.
n.13: Literally "to sit in a house".
n.14: Hebrew *tirzah*, a word found only here, perhaps a kind of cypress or holm oak.
n.15: Hebrew *oren*, perhaps a laurel, pine or cedar. In the Hebrew text one letter of this word (*nun*) is written small, a scribal mark.
n.16: Literally "their hearts".
n.17: Literally "No one brings it back to his heart".
n.18: Or "He tends ashes", as a shepherd tends a flock. Hebrew *ro'eh efer*.
n.19: Literally "his *nephesh*".
n.20: Or "you must not forget me". The Hebrew form is unusual.
n.21: The Hebrew text is written "Who was with me?" but read "by myself".
n.22: Hebrew *baddim*, "babblers", probably prophets who speak empty words, or diviners.
