v: The righteous one perishes, and no one takes it to heart. The faithful[^1] are taken away, and no one understands that the righteous one is taken away from the evil to come.[^2]
הַצַּדִּ֣יק אָבָ֔ד וְאֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ שָׂ֣ם עַל־לֵ֑ב וְאַנְשֵׁי־חֶ֤סֶד נֶֽאֱסָפִים֙ בְּאֵ֣ין מֵבִ֔ין כִּֽי־מִפְּנֵ֥י הָרָעָ֖ה נֶאֱסַ֥ף הַצַּדִּֽיק׃
He enters into peace; they rest on their beds,[^3] all who walk uprightly.
יָב֣וֹא שָׁל֔וֹם יָנ֖וּחוּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם הֹלֵ֖ךְ נְכֹחֽוֹ׃
But you, come here, you children of a sorceress, offspring of an adulterer and a prostitute!
וְאַתֶּ֥ם קִרְבוּ־הֵ֖נָּה בְּנֵ֣י עֹנְנָ֑ה זֶ֥רַע מְנָאֵ֖ף וַתִּזְנֶֽה׃
Whom are you mocking? At whom do you open your mouth wide and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of rebellion, offspring of deceit?
עַל־מִי֙ תִּתְעַנָּ֔גוּ עַל־מִ֛י תַּרְחִ֥יבוּ פֶ֖ה תַּאֲרִ֣יכוּ לָשׁ֑וֹן הֲלֽוֹא־אַתֶּ֥ם יִלְדֵי־פֶ֖שַׁע זֶ֥רַע שָֽׁקֶר׃
You inflame yourselves among the oaks,[^4] under every green tree; you slaughter children in the ravines, under the clefts of the rocks.[^5]
הַנֵּֽחָמִים֙ בָּֽאֵלִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת כָּל־עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֑ן שֹׁחֲטֵ֤י הַיְלָדִים֙ בַּנְּחָלִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת סְעִפֵ֥י הַסְּלָעִֽים׃

Among the smooth stones of the ravine is your portion;[^6] they, they are your lot. To them you have poured out drink offerings and brought up grain offerings.[^7] Should I relent because of these things?
בְּחַלְּקֵי־נַ֣חַל חֶלְקֵ֔ךְ הֵ֥ם הֵ֖ם גּוֹרָלֵ֑ךְ גַּם־לָהֶ֞ם שָׁפַ֥כְתְּ נֶ֙סֶךְ֙ הֶעֱלִ֣ית מִנְחָ֔ה הַ֥עַל אֵ֖לֶּה אֶנָּחֵֽם׃
On a high and lofty mountain you have made your bed; there too you went up to offer sacrifice.
עַ֤ל הַר־גָּבֹ֙הַּ֙ וְנִשָּׂ֔א שַׂ֖מְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבֵ֑ךְ גַּם־שָׁ֥ם עָלִ֖ית לִזְבֹּ֥חַ זָֽבַח׃

Behind the door and the doorpost you have set up your sign.[^8] For, deserting me, you uncovered your bed, climbed up into it and opened it wide. You made a bargain for yourself with them; you loved their bed; you gazed on their nakedness.[^9]
וְאַחַ֤ר הַדֶּ֙לֶת֙ וְהַמְּזוּזָ֔ה שַׂ֖מְתְּ זִכְרוֹנֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י מֵאִתִּ֞י גִּלִּ֣ית וַֽתַּעֲלִ֗י הִרְחַ֤בְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבֵךְ֙ וַתִּכְרָת־לָ֣ךְ מֵהֶ֔ם אָהַ֥בְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבָ֖ם יָ֥ד חָזִֽית׃
You went to the king[^10] with oil and gave him many perfumes. You sent your envoys far away; you sent them down even to Sheol.[^11]
וַתָּשֻׁ֤רִי לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וַתַּרְבִּ֖י רִקֻּחָ֑יִךְ וַתְּשַׁלְּחִ֤י צִרַ֙יִךְ֙ עַד־מֵ֣רָחֹ֔ק וַתַּשְׁפִּ֖ילִי עַד־שְׁאֽוֹל׃
You were wearied by your many journeys, but you did not say, "It is hopeless." You found new strength,[^12] so you did not grow faint.
בְּרֹ֤ב דַּרְכֵּךְ֙ יָגַ֔עַתְּ לֹ֥א אָמַ֖רְתְּ נוֹאָ֑שׁ חַיַּ֤ת יָדֵךְ֙ מָצָ֔את עַל־כֵּ֖ן לֹ֥א חָלִֽית׃
Whom did you dread and fear, that you lied, and did not remember me or take it to heart? Is it not because I have kept silent, and for a long time, that you do not fear me?
וְאֶת־מִ֞י דָּאַ֤גְתְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ כִּ֣י תְכַזֵּ֔בִי וְאוֹתִי֙ לֹ֣א זָכַ֔רְתְּ לֹא־שַׂ֖מְתְּ עַל־לִבֵּ֑ךְ הֲלֹ֨א אֲנִ֤י מַחְשֶׁה֙ וּמֵ֣עֹלָ֔ם וְאוֹתִ֖י לֹ֥א תִירָֽאִי׃
I will expose your righteousness and your deeds,[^13] and they will not help you.
אֲנִ֥י אַגִּ֖יד צִדְקָתֵ֑ךְ וְאֶֽת־מַעֲשַׂ֖יִךְ וְלֹ֥א יוֹעִילֽוּךְ׃

When you cry out, let your collection of idols[^14] save you! The wind will carry them all off; a breath will take them away. But whoever takes refuge in me will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain.
בְּזַֽעֲקֵךְ֙ יַצִּילֻ֣ךְ קִבּוּצַ֔יִךְ וְאֶת־כֻּלָּ֥ם יִשָּׂא־ר֖וּחַ יִקַּח־הָ֑בֶל וְהַחוֹסֶ֥ה בִי֙ יִנְחַל־אֶ֔רֶץ וְיִירַ֖שׁ הַר־קָדְשִֽׁי׃
And it will be said, "Build it up, build it up, prepare the road! Remove every obstacle from the way of my people."
וְאָמַ֥ר סֹֽלּוּ־סֹ֖לּוּ פַּנּוּ־דָ֑רֶךְ הָרִ֥ימוּ מִכְשׁ֖וֹל מִדֶּ֥רֶךְ עַמִּֽי׃ ס

For this is what the High and Lofty One says, who lives forever,[^15] whose name is Holy: I live in a high and holy place, and also with the one who is crushed and humble in spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble and to revive the heart of the crushed.
כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֗א שֹׁכֵ֥ן עַד֙ וְקָד֣וֹשׁ שְׁמ֔וֹ מָר֥וֹם וְקָד֖וֹשׁ אֶשְׁכּ֑וֹן וְאֶת־דַּכָּא֙ וּשְׁפַל־ר֔וּחַ לְהַחֲיוֹת֙ ר֣וּחַ שְׁפָלִ֔ים וּֽלְהַחֲי֖וֹת לֵ֥ב נִדְכָּאִֽים׃
For I will not accuse forever, nor will I always be angry. For then the spirit[^16] would grow faint before me, the breath of life that I have made.
כִּ֣י לֹ֤א לְעוֹלָם֙ אָרִ֔יב וְלֹ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח אֶקְּצ֑וֹף כִּי־ר֙וּחַ֙ מִלְּפָנַ֣י יַֽעֲט֔וֹף וּנְשָׁמ֖וֹת אֲנִ֥י עָשִֽׂיתִי׃
Because of the guilt of his greed I was angry, and I struck him; I hid my face and was angry. But he went on turning away, in the way of his own heart.
בַּעֲוֺ֥ן בִּצְע֛וֹ קָצַ֥פְתִּי וְאַכֵּ֖הוּ הַסְתֵּ֣ר וְאֶקְצֹ֑ף וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ שׁוֹבָ֖ב בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ לִבּֽוֹ׃
I have seen his ways, but I will heal him. I will lead him and repay him with comfort, him and those who mourn for him,
דְּרָכָ֥יו רָאִ֖יתִי וְאֶרְפָּאֵ֑הוּ וְאַנְחֵ֕הוּ וַאֲשַׁלֵּ֧ם נִֽחֻמִ֛ים ל֖וֹ וְלַאֲבֵלָֽיו׃
creating praise on their lips:[^17] Peace, peace, to the far and to the near, says the LORD,[^18] and I will heal him.[^19]
בּוֹרֵ֖א *נוב **נִ֣יב שְׂפָתָ֑יִם שָׁל֨וֹם ׀ שָׁל֜וֹם לָרָח֧וֹק וְלַקָּר֛וֹב אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה וּרְפָאתִֽיו׃
But the wicked are like the tossing sea, which cannot be still; its waters toss up mud and mire.
וְהָרְשָׁעִ֖ים כַּיָּ֣ם נִגְרָ֑שׁ כִּ֤י הַשְׁקֵט֙ לֹ֣א יוּכָ֔ל וַיִּגְרְשׁ֥וּ מֵימָ֖יו רֶ֥פֶשׁ וָטִֽיט׃
There is no peace, says my God, for the wicked.[^20]
אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י לָרְשָׁעִֽים׃ ס

n.1: Literally "men of *chesed*", those who show faithful love.
n.2: Literally "from before the evil". Or "because of the evil": the righteous are removed by the wrongdoing of others, or spared the disaster that is coming.
n.3: Their graves.
n.4: Or "with the gods". Hebrew *elim*, "sacred trees" (1:29), can also mean "gods". *You* is plural in verses 3–5, then feminine singular in verses 6–13, as the people are addressed as an unfaithful wife.
n.5: Children were sacrificed to other gods in the Valley of Ben-hinnom near Jerusalem (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31).
n.6: A play on words: *chalqe nachal*, "the smooth stones of the ravine", and *chelqekh*, "your portion". The smooth stones may have been objects of worship.
n.7: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute", in Leviticus a grain offering.
n.8: Hebrew *zikkaron*, "memorial, reminder", perhaps a pagan symbol placed where the words of the LORD's law were to be written (Deuteronomy 6:9).
n.9: Literally "you saw a hand". *Hand* (Hebrew *yad*) may be a polite word for the male organ, or mean a memorial pillar (56:5).
n.10: Or "to Molech", the god to whom children were sacrificed (Leviticus 18:21), whose name sounds like *melekh*, "king".
n.11: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.12: Literally "You found the life of your hand".
n.13: The words are said with irony: what they call righteousness will be shown for what it is.
n.14: Literally "your collections", perhaps a gathering of idols or of foreign allies.
n.15: Or "who inhabits eternity". The words *high and lofty* are the "high and lifted up" of 6:1 and 52:13.
n.16: Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, breath", in parallel with *neshamot*, "breaths".
n.17: Literally "creating the fruit of the lips". Compare Hebrews 13:15.
n.18: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.19: Ephesians 2:17 echoes this verse.
n.20: This line repeats 48:22, with "my God" instead of "the LORD".

v: Shout aloud;[^1] do not hold back! Raise your voice like a ram's horn! Declare to my people their rebellion, and to the house of Jacob their sins.
קְרָ֤א בְגָרוֹן֙ אַל־תַּחְשֹׂ֔ךְ כַּשּׁוֹפָ֖ר הָרֵ֣ם קוֹלֶ֑ךָ וְהַגֵּ֤ד לְעַמִּי֙ פִּשְׁעָ֔ם וּלְבֵ֥ית יַעֲקֹ֖ב חַטֹּאתָֽם׃

Yet day after day they seek me and delight to know my ways, as if they were a nation that did what is right and had not abandoned the justice of its God. They ask me for righteous judgments; they delight in drawing near to God.

וְאוֹתִ֗י י֥וֹם יוֹם֙ יִדְרֹשׁ֔וּן וְדַ֥עַת דְּרָכַ֖י יֶחְפָּצ֑וּן כְּג֞וֹי אֲשֶׁר־צְדָקָ֣ה עָשָׂ֗ה וּמִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֱלֹהָיו֙ לֹ֣א עָזָ֔ב יִשְׁאָל֙וּנִי֙ מִשְׁפְּטֵי־צֶ֔דֶק קִרְבַ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֶחְפָּצֽוּן׃

"Why have we fasted," they say, "and you do not see? Why have we denied ourselves,[^2] and you do not notice?" Look, on the day of your fast you pursue your own business and drive all your workers hard.[^3]
לָ֤מָּה צַּ֙מְנוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א רָאִ֔יתָ עִנִּ֥ינוּ נַפְשֵׁ֖נוּ וְלֹ֣א תֵדָ֑ע הֵ֣ן בְּי֤וֹם צֹֽמְכֶם֙ תִּמְצְאוּ־חֵ֔פֶץ וְכָל־עַצְּבֵיכֶ֖ם תִּנְגֹּֽשׂוּ׃
Look, you fast only to quarrel and fight and to strike with a wicked fist. You cannot fast as you do today and make your voice heard on high.
הֵ֣ן לְרִ֤יב וּמַצָּה֙ תָּצ֔וּמוּ וּלְהַכּ֖וֹת בְּאֶגְרֹ֣ף רֶ֑שַׁע לֹא־תָצ֣וּמוּ כַיּ֔וֹם לְהַשְׁמִ֥יעַ בַּמָּר֖וֹם קוֹלְכֶֽם׃

Is this the kind of fast I choose, a day for a person to deny himself? Is it to bow one's head like a reed and to lie on sackcloth and ashes? Is this what you call a fast, a day acceptable to the LORD?[^4]
הֲכָזֶ֗ה יִֽהְיֶה֙ צ֣וֹם אֶבְחָרֵ֔הוּ י֛וֹם עַנּ֥וֹת אָדָ֖ם נַפְשׁ֑וֹ הֲלָכֹ֨ף כְּאַגְמֹ֜ן רֹאשׁ֗וֹ וְשַׂ֤ק וָאֵ֙פֶר֙ יַצִּ֔יעַ הֲלָזֶה֙ תִּקְרָא־צ֔וֹם וְי֥וֹם רָצ֖וֹן לַיהוָֽה׃
Is not this the fast that I choose: to loosen the chains of wickedness, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free and to break every yoke?
הֲל֣וֹא זֶה֮ צ֣וֹם אֶבְחָרֵהוּ֒ פַּתֵּ֙חַ֙ חַרְצֻבּ֣וֹת רֶ֔שַׁע הַתֵּ֖ר אֲגֻדּ֣וֹת מוֹטָ֑ה וְשַׁלַּ֤ח רְצוּצִים֙ חָפְשִׁ֔ים וְכָל־מוֹטָ֖ה תְּנַתֵּֽקוּ׃
Is it not to share your bread with the hungry and to bring the homeless poor into your house, to cover the naked when you see them, and not to turn away from your own flesh and blood?[^5]
הֲל֨וֹא פָרֹ֤ס לָֽרָעֵב֙ לַחְמֶ֔ךָ וַעֲנִיִּ֥ים מְרוּדִ֖ים תָּ֣בִיא בָ֑יִת כִּֽי־תִרְאֶ֤ה עָרֹם֙ וְכִסִּית֔וֹ וּמִבְּשָׂרְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תִתְעַלָּֽם׃
Then your light will break out like the dawn, and your healing will spring up quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will be your rear guard.[^6]
אָ֣ז יִבָּקַ֤ע כַּשַּׁ֙חַר֙ אוֹרֶ֔ךָ וַאֲרֻכָתְךָ֖ מְהֵרָ֣ה תִצְמָ֑ח וְהָלַ֤ךְ לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ צִדְקֶ֔ךָ כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה יַאַסְפֶֽךָ׃
Then you will call, and the LORD will answer; you will cry for help, and he will say, "Here I am." If you remove the yoke from among you, the pointing finger and wicked speech,
אָ֤ז תִּקְרָא֙ וַיהוָ֣ה יַעֲנֶ֔ה תְּשַׁוַּ֖ע וְיֹאמַ֣ר הִנֵּ֑נִי אִם־תָּסִ֤יר מִתּֽוֹכְךָ֙ מוֹטָ֔ה שְׁלַ֥ח אֶצְבַּ֖ע וְדַבֶּר־אָֽוֶן׃
if you pour yourself out[^7] for the hungry and satisfy the needs of the afflicted, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your gloom will be like noon.
וְתָפֵ֤ק לָֽרָעֵב֙ נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ נַעֲנָ֖ה תַּשְׂבִּ֑יעַ וְזָרַ֤ח בַּחֹ֙שֶׁךְ֙ אוֹרֶ֔ךָ וַאֲפֵלָתְךָ֖ כַּֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃
The LORD will guide you always and satisfy your needs[^8] in parched places and strengthen your bones. You will be like a watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
וְנָחֲךָ֣ יְהוָה֮ תָּמִיד֒ וְהִשְׂבִּ֤יעַ בְּצַחְצָחוֹת֙ נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ וְעַצְמֹתֶ֖יךָ יַחֲלִ֑יץ וְהָיִ֙יתָ֙ כְּגַ֣ן רָוֶ֔ה וּכְמוֹצָ֣א מַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יְכַזְּב֖וּ מֵימָֽיו׃
Your people[^9] will rebuild the ancient ruins; you will raise up the foundations of many generations. You will be called the Repairer of the Breach, the Restorer of Streets to Live In.
וּבָנ֤וּ מִמְּךָ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם מוֹסְדֵ֥י דוֹר־וָד֖וֹר תְּקוֹמֵ֑ם וְקֹרָ֤א לְךָ֙ גֹּדֵ֣ר פֶּ֔רֶץ מְשֹׁבֵ֥ב נְתִיב֖וֹת לָשָֽׁבֶת׃

If you keep your feet from trampling the Sabbath,[^10] from doing as you please on my holy day; if you call the Sabbath a delight and the holy day of the LORD honored; if you honor it by not going your own ways, not pursuing your own business or speaking idle words,[^11]

אִם־תָּשִׁ֤יב מִשַּׁבָּת֙ רַגְלֶ֔ךָ עֲשׂ֥וֹת חֲפָצֶ֖יךָ בְּי֣וֹם קָדְשִׁ֑י וְקָרָ֨אתָ לַשַּׁבָּ֜ת עֹ֗נֶג לִקְד֤וֹשׁ יְהוָה֙ מְכֻבָּ֔ד וְכִבַּדְתּוֹ֙ מֵעֲשׂ֣וֹת דְּרָכֶ֔יךָ מִמְּצ֥וֹא חֶפְצְךָ֖ וְדַבֵּ֥ר דָּבָֽר׃

then you will find your delight in the LORD, and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth[^12] and feed you with the inheritance of your ancestor Jacob.[^13] For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
אָ֗ז תִּתְעַנַּג֙ עַל־יְהוָ֔ה וְהִרְכַּבְתִּ֖יךָ עַל־בָּ֣מֳותֵי אָ֑רֶץ וְהַאֲכַלְתִּ֗יךָ נַחֲלַת֙ יַעֲקֹ֣ב אָבִ֔יךָ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ ס

n.1: Literally "Call with the throat".
n.2: Literally "humbled our *nephesh*", the phrase used for fasting on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29, 31). Also in verses 5 and 10.
n.3: Or "and exact all your debts". Hebrew *atsevekhem*, perhaps "your laborers" or "your loans".
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Literally "from your own flesh", your relatives and fellow Israelites.
n.6: Compare 52:12, and the pillar of cloud and fire that went before and behind Israel (Exodus 14:19–20).
n.7: Literally "if you offer your *nephesh*". *The needs of the afflicted* is literally "the afflicted *nephesh*".
n.8: Literally "satisfy your *nephesh*". Hebrew *tsachtsachot*, "parched places", is found only here.
n.9: Literally "those from you".
n.10: Literally "If you turn back your foot from the Sabbath".
n.11: Literally "or speaking a word". *Your own business* is the phrase translated "your own business" in verse 3.
n.12: Compare Deuteronomy 32:13.
n.13: Literally "Jacob your father".

v: Look, the hand of the LORD[^1] is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear.
הֵ֛ן לֹֽא־קָצְרָ֥ה יַד־יְהוָ֖ה מֵֽהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ וְלֹא־כָבְדָ֥ה אָזְנ֖וֹ מִשְּׁמֽוֹעַ׃
But your wrongdoings have separated you from your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he does not hear.
כִּ֤י אִם־עֲוֺנֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ הָי֣וּ מַבְדִּלִ֔ים בֵּינֵכֶ֕ם לְבֵ֖ין אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֑ם וְחַטֹּֽאותֵיכֶ֗ם הִסְתִּ֧ירוּ פָנִ֛ים מִכֶּ֖ם מִשְּׁמֽוֹעַ׃
For your hands are defiled with blood and your fingers with guilt. Your lips have spoken lies; your tongue mutters wickedness.
כִּ֤י כַפֵּיכֶם֙ נְגֹאֲל֣וּ בַדָּ֔ם וְאֶצְבְּעוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם בֶּֽעָוֺ֑ן שִׂפְתֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ דִּבְּרוּ־שֶׁ֔קֶר לְשׁוֹנְכֶ֖ם עַוְלָ֥ה תֶהְגֶּֽה׃
No one brings a case justly;[^2] no one goes to law honestly. They trust in empty words and speak lies; they conceive trouble and give birth to evil.
אֵין־קֹרֵ֣א בְצֶ֔דֶק וְאֵ֥ין נִשְׁפָּ֖ט בֶּאֱמוּנָ֑ה בָּט֤וֹחַ עַל־תֹּ֙הוּ֙ וְדַבֶּר־שָׁ֔וְא הָר֥וֹ עָמָ֖ל וְהוֹלֵ֥יד אָֽוֶן׃
They hatch the eggs of vipers and weave spiders' webs. Whoever eats their eggs dies, and when one is crushed, a snake hatches out.
בֵּיצֵ֤י צִפְעוֹנִי֙ בִּקֵּ֔עוּ וְקוּרֵ֥י עַכָּבִ֖ישׁ יֶאֱרֹ֑גוּ הָאֹכֵ֤ל מִבֵּֽיצֵיהֶם֙ יָמ֔וּת וְהַזּוּרֶ֖ה תִּבָּקַ֥ע אֶפְעֶֽה׃
Their webs will not become clothing; they cannot cover themselves with what they make. Their works are works of evil, and acts of violence are in their hands.
קֽוּרֵיהֶם֙ לֹא־יִהְי֣וּ לְבֶ֔גֶד וְלֹ֥א יִתְכַּסּ֖וּ בְּמַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ מַֽעֲשֵׂי־אָ֔וֶן וּפֹ֥עַל חָמָ֖ס בְּכַפֵּיהֶֽם׃
Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of evil; ruin and destruction are on their highways.
רַגְלֵיהֶם֙ לָרַ֣ע יָרֻ֔צוּ וִֽימַהֲר֔וּ לִשְׁפֹּ֖ךְ דָּ֣ם נָקִ֑י מַחְשְׁבֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת אָ֔וֶן שֹׁ֥ד וָשֶׁ֖בֶר בִּמְסִלּוֹתָֽם׃
They do not know the way of peace, and there is no justice in their tracks. They have made their paths crooked; no one who walks on them knows peace.[^3]
דֶּ֤רֶךְ שָׁלוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם נְתִיבֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ עִקְּשׁ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם כֹּ֚ל דֹּרֵ֣ךְ בָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א יָדַ֖ע שָׁלֽוֹם׃
That is why justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We hope for light, but look, there is darkness; for brightness, but we walk in gloom.
עַל־כֵּ֗ן רָחַ֤ק מִשְׁפָּט֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תַשִּׂיגֵ֖נוּ צְדָקָ֑ה נְקַוֶּ֤ה לָאוֹר֙ וְהִנֵּה־חֹ֔שֶׁךְ לִנְגֹה֖וֹת בָּאֲפֵל֥וֹת נְהַלֵּֽךְ׃
We grope along the wall like the blind; we grope like those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as in the twilight; among the strong we are like the dead.[^4]
נְגַֽשְׁשָׁ֤ה כַֽעִוְרִים֙ קִ֔יר וּכְאֵ֥ין עֵינַ֖יִם נְגַשֵּׁ֑שָׁה כָּשַׁ֤לְנוּ בַֽצָּהֳרַ֙יִם֙ כַּנֶּ֔שֶׁף בָּאַשְׁמַנִּ֖ים כַּמֵּתִֽים׃
We all growl like bears; we moan and moan like doves. We hope for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far from us.
נֶהֱמֶ֤ה כַדֻּבִּים֙ כֻּלָּ֔נוּ וְכַיּוֹנִ֖ים הָגֹ֣ה נֶהְגֶּ֑ה נְקַוֶּ֤ה לַמִּשְׁפָּט֙ וָאַ֔יִן לִֽישׁוּעָ֖ה רָחֲקָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
For our rebellious acts are many before you, and our sins testify against us. Our rebellious acts are with us, and we know our wrongdoings:
כִּֽי־רַבּ֤וּ פְשָׁעֵ֙ינוּ֙ נֶגְדֶּ֔ךָ וְחַטֹּאותֵ֖ינוּ עָ֣נְתָה בָּ֑נוּ כִּֽי־פְשָׁעֵ֣ינוּ אִתָּ֔נוּ וַעֲוֺנֹתֵ֖ינוּ יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם׃
rebelling and denying the LORD, turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering lies from the heart.
פָּשֹׁ֤עַ וְכַחֵשׁ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וְנָס֖וֹג מֵאַחַ֣ר אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ דַּבֶּר־עֹ֣שֶׁק וְסָרָ֔ה הֹר֧וֹ וְהֹג֛וֹ מִלֵּ֖ב דִּבְרֵי־שָֽׁקֶר׃
So justice is driven back, and righteousness stands far away. Truth has stumbled in the public square, and honesty cannot enter.
וְהֻסַּ֤ג אָחוֹר֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה מֵרָח֣וֹק תַּעֲמֹ֑ד כִּֽי־כָשְׁלָ֤ה בָֽרְחוֹב֙ אֱמֶ֔ת וּנְכֹחָ֖ה לֹא־תוּכַ֥ל לָבֽוֹא׃
Truth is missing, and whoever turns away from evil makes himself a prey. The LORD saw it, and it was evil in his eyes that there was no justice.
וַתְּהִ֤י הָֽאֱמֶת֙ נֶעְדֶּ֔רֶת וְסָ֥ר מֵרָ֖ע מִשְׁתּוֹלֵ֑ל וַיַּ֧רְא יְהוָ֛ה וַיֵּ֥רַע בְּעֵינָ֖יו כִּֽי־אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
He saw that there was no one; he was appalled that there was no one to intervene.[^5] So his own arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness upheld him.
וַיַּרְא֙ כִּֽי־אֵ֣ין אִ֔ישׁ וַיִּשְׁתּוֹמֵ֖ם כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין מַפְגִּ֑יעַ וַתּ֤וֹשַֽׁע לוֹ֙ זְרֹע֔וֹ וְצִדְקָת֖וֹ הִ֥יא סְמָכָֽתְהוּ׃
He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on his head. He put on garments of vengeance for clothing and wrapped himself in zeal as in a cloak.[^6]
וַיִּלְבַּ֤שׁ צְדָקָה֙ כַּשִּׁרְיָ֔ן וְכ֥וֹבַע יְשׁוּעָ֖ה בְּרֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּלְבַּ֞שׁ בִּגְדֵ֤י נָקָם֙ תִּלְבֹּ֔שֶׁת וַיַּ֥עַט כַּמְעִ֖יל קִנְאָֽה׃
According to what they have done, so he will repay: fury to his adversaries, retribution to his enemies; to the coastlands[^7] he will repay retribution.
כְּעַ֤ל גְּמֻלוֹת֙ כְּעַ֣ל יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם חֵמָ֣ה לְצָרָ֔יו גְּמ֖וּל לְאֹֽיְבָ֑יו לָאִיִּ֖ים גְּמ֥וּל יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃
So from the west they will fear the name of the LORD, and from the rising of the sun his glory. For he will come like a rushing river, driven by the wind of the LORD.[^8]
וְיִֽירְא֤וּ מִֽמַּעֲרָב֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּמִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ אֶת־כְּבוֹד֑וֹ כִּֽי־יָב֤וֹא כַנָּהָר֙ צָ֔ר ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה נֹ֥סְסָה בֽוֹ׃
A Redeemer[^9] will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from rebellion, declares the LORD.[^10]
וּבָ֤א לְצִיּוֹן֙ גּוֹאֵ֔ל וּלְשָׁבֵ֥י פֶ֖שַׁע בְּיַֽעֲקֹ֑ב נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃

As for me, this is my covenant with them, says the LORD: My Spirit, who is on you, and my words that I have put in your mouth will not depart from your mouth, or from the mouths of your children, or from the mouths of your children's children, says the LORD, from now on and forever.

וַאֲנִ֗י זֹ֣את בְּרִיתִ֤י אוֹתָם֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה רוּחִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלֶ֔יךָ וּדְבָרַ֖י אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֣מְתִּי בְּפִ֑יךָ לֹֽא־יָמ֡וּשׁוּ מִפִּיךָ֩ וּמִפִּ֨י זַרְעֲךָ֜ וּמִפִּ֨י זֶ֤רַע זַרְעֲךָ֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַתָּ֖ה וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "No one calls in righteousness".
n.3: Romans 3:15–17 quotes verses 7–8 from the Septuagint.
n.4: Hebrew *ashmannim*, a word found only here, perhaps "among the vigorous" or "in desolate places".
n.5: Hebrew *mafgia*, the verb translated "made intercession" in 53:12.
n.6: Paul takes up the images of this verse in Ephesians 6:14–17 and 1 Thessalonians 5:8.
n.7: Hebrew *iyyim*, the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean (11:11), and in these chapters the most distant lands.
n.8: Or "breath" or "Spirit". Hebrew *ruach*. Literally "like a narrow river, the wind of the LORD driving it". The words can also be read "When the enemy comes like a river, the Spirit of the LORD will raise a banner against him", taking *tsar* as "enemy" and *nosesah* from *nes*, "banner".
n.9: Hebrew *go'el* (41:14).
n.10: Romans 11:26–27 quotes verses 20–21 from the Septuagint: "The Deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob. And this will be my covenant with them."

v: Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD[^1] has risen on you.
ק֥וּמִי א֖וֹרִי כִּ֣י בָ֣א אוֹרֵ֑ךְ וּכְב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה עָלַ֥יִךְ זָרָֽח׃
For look, darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness the peoples. But the LORD rises on you, and his glory appears over you.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה הַחֹ֙שֶׁךְ֙ יְכַסֶּה־אֶ֔רֶץ וַעֲרָפֶ֖ל לְאֻמִּ֑ים וְעָלַ֙יִךְ֙ יִזְרַ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה וּכְבוֹד֖וֹ עָלַ֥יִךְ יֵרָאֶֽה׃
Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
וְהָלְכ֥וּ גוֹיִ֖ם לְאוֹרֵ֑ךְ וּמְלָכִ֖ים לְנֹ֥גַהּ זַרְחֵֽךְ׃
Lift up your eyes and look around: they all gather and come to you. Your sons will come from far away, and your daughters will be carried on the hip.[^2]
שְׂאִֽי־סָבִ֤יב עֵינַ֙יִךְ֙ וּרְאִ֔י כֻּלָּ֖ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ בָֽאוּ־לָ֑ךְ בָּנַ֙יִךְ֙ מֵרָח֣וֹק יָבֹ֔אוּ וּבְנֹתַ֖יִךְ עַל־צַ֥ד תֵּאָמַֽנָה׃
Then you will see and be radiant; your heart will throb and swell with joy,[^3] for the abundance of the sea will be turned to you, and the wealth of the nations will come to you.
אָ֤ז תִּרְאִי֙ וְנָהַ֔רְתְּ וּפָחַ֥ד וְרָחַ֖ב לְבָבֵ֑ךְ כִּֽי־יֵהָפֵ֤ךְ עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ הֲמ֣וֹן יָ֔ם חֵ֥יל גּוֹיִ֖ם יָבֹ֥אוּ לָֽךְ׃
A multitude of camels will cover you, young camels of Midian and Ephah. All those from Sheba will come, bringing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the LORD.[^4]
שִֽׁפְעַ֨ת גְּמַלִּ֜ים תְּכַסֵּ֗ךְ בִּכְרֵ֤י מִדְיָן֙ וְעֵיפָ֔ה כֻּלָּ֖ם מִשְּׁבָ֣א יָבֹ֑אוּ זָהָ֤ב וּלְבוֹנָה֙ יִשָּׂ֔אוּ וּתְהִלֹּ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה יְבַשֵּֽׂרוּ׃
All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth[^5] will serve you. They will go up as acceptable offerings on my altar, and I will make my glorious house more glorious still.
כָּל־צֹ֤אן קֵדָר֙ יִקָּ֣בְצוּ לָ֔ךְ אֵילֵ֥י נְבָי֖וֹת יְשָׁרְת֑וּנֶךְ יַעֲל֤וּ עַל־רָצוֹן֙ מִזְבְּחִ֔י וּבֵ֥ית תִּפְאַרְתִּ֖י אֲפָאֵֽר׃
Who are these that fly like a cloud, like doves to their windows?[^6]
מִי־אֵ֖לֶּה כָּעָ֣ב תְּעוּפֶ֑ינָה וְכַיּוֹנִ֖ים אֶל־אֲרֻבֹּתֵיהֶֽם׃

Surely the coastlands[^7] wait for me, with the ships of Tarshish[^8] in the lead, to bring your sons from far away, their silver and gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God, for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.

כִּֽי־לִ֣י ׀ אִיִּ֣ים יְקַוּ֗וּ וָאֳנִיּ֤וֹת תַּרְשִׁישׁ֙ בָּרִ֣אשֹׁנָ֔ה לְהָבִ֤יא בָנַ֙יִךְ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק כַּסְפָּ֥ם וּזְהָבָ֖ם אִתָּ֑ם לְשֵׁם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִךְ וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֥י פֵאֲרָֽךְ׃
Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. For in my anger I struck you, but in my favor I have had compassion on you.
וּבָנ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־נֵכָר֙ חֹמֹתַ֔יִךְ וּמַלְכֵיהֶ֖ם יְשָׁרְת֑וּנֶךְ כִּ֤י בְקִצְפִּי֙ הִכִּיתִ֔יךְ וּבִרְצוֹנִ֖י רִֽחַמְתִּֽיךְ׃
Your gates will always stand open; day and night they will not be shut, so that people may bring you the wealth of the nations, with their kings led in procession.[^9]
וּפִתְּח֨וּ שְׁעָרַ֧יִךְ תָּמִ֛יד יוֹמָ֥ם וָלַ֖יְלָה לֹ֣א יִסָּגֵ֑רוּ לְהָבִ֤יא אֵלַ֙יִךְ֙ חֵ֣יל גּוֹיִ֔ם וּמַלְכֵיהֶ֖ם נְהוּגִֽים׃
For the nation or kingdom that will not serve you will perish; those nations will be utterly ruined.
כִּֽי־הַגּ֧וֹי וְהַמַּמְלָכָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יַעַבְד֖וּךְ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ וְהַגּוֹיִ֖ם חָרֹ֥ב יֶחֱרָֽבוּ׃
The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the juniper, the plane tree and the pine together,[^10] to beautify the place of my sanctuary, and I will make the place of my feet glorious.
כְּב֤וֹד הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ אֵלַ֣יִךְ יָב֔וֹא בְּר֛וֹשׁ תִּדְהָ֥ר וּתְאַשּׁ֖וּר יַחְדָּ֑ו לְפָאֵר֙ מְק֣וֹם מִקְדָּשִׁ֔י וּמְק֥וֹם רַגְלַ֖י אֲכַבֵּֽד׃

The sons of those who oppressed you will come bowing low to you, and all who despised you will bow down at the soles of your feet.[^11] They will call you the City of the LORD, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
וְהָלְכ֨וּ אֵלַ֤יִךְ שְׁח֙וֹחַ֙ בְּנֵ֣י מְעַנַּ֔יִךְ וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ עַל־כַּפּ֥וֹת רַגְלַ֖יִךְ כָּל־מְנַֽאֲצָ֑יִךְ וְקָ֤רְאוּ לָךְ֙ עִ֣יר יְהוָ֔ה צִיּ֖וֹן קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Instead of being abandoned and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from generation to generation.
תַּ֧חַת הֱיוֹתֵ֛ךְ עֲזוּבָ֥ה וּשְׂנוּאָ֖ה וְאֵ֣ין עוֹבֵ֑ר וְשַׂמְתִּיךְ֙ לִגְא֣וֹן עוֹלָ֔ם מְשׂ֖וֹשׂ דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃
You will drink the milk of nations and nurse at the breasts of kings. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer,[^12] the Mighty One of Jacob.
וְיָנַקְתְּ֙ חֲלֵ֣ב גּוֹיִ֔ם וְשֹׁ֥ד מְלָכִ֖ים תִּינָ֑קִי וְיָדַ֗עַתְּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ אֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב׃
Instead of bronze I will bring gold, and instead of iron I will bring silver; instead of wood, bronze, and instead of stones, iron. I will make peace your overseer and righteousness your ruler.[^13]
תַּ֣חַת הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת אָבִ֣יא זָהָ֗ב וְתַ֤חַת הַבַּרְזֶל֙ אָ֣בִיא כֶ֔סֶף וְתַ֤חַת הָֽעֵצִים֙ נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וְתַ֥חַת הָאֲבָנִ֖ים בַּרְזֶ֑ל וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י פְקֻדָּתֵךְ֙ שָׁל֔וֹם וְנֹגְשַׂ֖יִךְ צְדָקָֽה׃
Violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor ruin or destruction within your borders. You will call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
לֹא־יִשָּׁמַ֨ע ע֤וֹד חָמָס֙ בְּאַרְצֵ֔ךְ שֹׁ֥ד וָשֶׁ֖בֶר בִּגְבוּלָ֑יִךְ וְקָרָ֤את יְשׁוּעָה֙ חוֹמֹתַ֔יִךְ וּשְׁעָרַ֖יִךְ תְּהִלָּֽה׃
The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon shine on you. But the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.[^14]
לֹא־יִֽהְיֶה־לָּ֨ךְ ע֤וֹד הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ לְא֣וֹר יוֹמָ֔ם וּלְנֹ֕גַהּ הַיָּרֵ֖חַ לֹא־יָאִ֣יר לָ֑ךְ וְהָיָה־לָ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ לְא֣וֹר עוֹלָ֔ם וֵאלֹהַ֖יִךְ לְתִפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ׃
Your sun will never set again, and your moon will not wane,[^15] for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be over.
לֹא־יָב֥וֹא עוֹד֙ שִׁמְשֵׁ֔ךְ וִירֵחֵ֖ךְ לֹ֣א יֵאָסֵ֑ף כִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה יִֽהְיֶה־לָּךְ֙ לְא֣וֹר עוֹלָ֔ם וְשָׁלְמ֖וּ יְמֵ֥י אֶבְלֵֽךְ׃
Your people will all be righteous; they will possess the land forever. They are the shoot I planted,[^16] the work of my hands, so that I may be glorified.
וְעַמֵּךְ֙ כֻּלָּ֣ם צַדִּיקִ֔ים לְעוֹלָ֖ם יִ֣ירְשׁוּ אָ֑רֶץ נֵ֧צֶר *מטעו **מַטָּעַ֛י מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֖י לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר׃
The least of them will become a thousand, and the smallest a mighty nation. I am the LORD; when the time comes, I will do this quickly.
הַקָּטֹן֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָאֶ֔לֶף וְהַצָּעִ֖יר לְג֣וֹי עָצ֑וּם אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּעִתָּ֥הּ אֲחִישֶֽׁנָּה׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *You* is feminine singular in this chapter: Zion is addressed as a woman (verse 14).
n.2: Literally "will be nursed on the side", carried as small children are carried.
n.3: Literally "your heart will tremble and grow wide".
n.4: Midian and Ephah were Arabian tribes descended from Abraham (Genesis 25:2–4), and Sheba was a kingdom in southern Arabia famous for its trade in gold and spices (1 Kings 10:1–2). Compare the gifts of the wise men in Matthew 2:11.
n.5: Kedar and Nebaioth were Arabian tribes, named as sons of Ishmael in Genesis 25:13.
n.6: Hebrew *arubbot*, "openings, lattices", perhaps the holes of a dovecote.
n.7: Hebrew *iyyim*, the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean (11:11), and in these chapters the most distant lands.
n.8: Large seagoing ships (2:16), of the kind that sailed to Tarshish, a distant port in the west.
n.9: Revelation 21:24–26 echoes verses 3 and 11.
n.10: The trees named in 41:19. Their identification is uncertain.
n.11: Revelation 3:9 echoes this line.
n.12: Hebrew *go'el* (41:14). The line repeats 49:26.
n.13: *Overseer* and *ruler* are the officials who once oppressed the people. Hebrew *noges* is the word for the slave drivers of Egypt (Exodus 3:7).
n.14: Revelation 21:23 and 22:5 echo verses 19–20.
n.15: Literally "will not be withdrawn".
n.16: Literally "the shoot of my planting". Hebrew *netser*, the word for the "branch" in 11:1. The Hebrew text is written "his planting" but read "my planting".

v: The Spirit[^1] of the Lord GOD[^2] is on me, because the LORD has anointed me[^3] to bring good news[^4] to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom[^5] for the captives and release for the prisoners,[^6]
ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י יַ֡עַן מָשַׁח֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֹתִ֜י לְבַשֵּׂ֣ר עֲנָוִ֗ים שְׁלָחַ֙נִי֙ לַחֲבֹ֣שׁ לְנִשְׁבְּרֵי־לֵ֔ב לִקְרֹ֤א לִשְׁבוּיִם֙ דְּר֔וֹר וְלַאֲסוּרִ֖ים פְּקַח־קֽוֹחַ׃
to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor and the day of vengeance of our God,[^7] to comfort all who mourn,
לִקְרֹ֤א שְׁנַת־רָצוֹן֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְי֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם לֵאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לְנַחֵ֖ם כָּל־אֲבֵלִֽים׃

to provide for those who mourn in Zion: to give them a garland instead of ashes,[^8] the oil of gladness instead of mourning, a garment of praise instead of a fainting spirit. They will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, so that he may be glorified.

לָשׂ֣וּם ׀ לַאֲבֵלֵ֣י צִיּ֗וֹן לָתֵת֩ לָהֶ֨ם פְּאֵ֜ר תַּ֣חַת אֵ֗פֶר שֶׁ֤מֶן שָׂשׂוֹן֙ תַּ֣חַת אֵ֔בֶל מַעֲטֵ֣ה תְהִלָּ֔ה תַּ֖חַת ר֣וּחַ כֵּהָ֑ה וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר׃
They will rebuild the ancient ruins and raise up the places long desolate. They will renew the ruined cities, the places desolate for generations.
וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃
Strangers will stand and tend your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and vinedressers.
וְעָמְד֣וּ זָרִ֔ים וְרָע֖וּ צֹאנְכֶ֑ם וּבְנֵ֣י נֵכָ֔ר אִכָּרֵיכֶ֖ם וְכֹרְמֵיכֶֽם׃
But you will be called priests of the LORD; you will be named ministers of our God.[^9] You will eat the wealth of the nations, and you will glory in their riches.
וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ תִּקָּרֵ֔אוּ מְשָׁרְתֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ יֵאָמֵ֖ר לָכֶ֑ם חֵ֤יל גּוֹיִם֙ תֹּאכֵ֔לוּ וּבִכְבוֹדָ֖ם תִּתְיַמָּֽרוּ׃

Instead of your shame you will have a double portion, and instead of disgrace they will rejoice in their lot.[^10] Therefore in their land they will possess a double portion; everlasting joy will be theirs.
תַּ֤חַת בָּשְׁתְּכֶם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֔ה וּכְלִמָּ֖ה יָרֹ֣נּוּ חֶלְקָ֑ם לָכֵ֤ן בְּאַרְצָם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֣ה יִירָ֔שׁוּ שִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶֽם׃
For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and wrongdoing.[^11] I will faithfully give them their reward and make an everlasting covenant with them.
כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֹהֵ֣ב מִשְׁפָּ֔ט שֹׂנֵ֥א גָזֵ֖ל בְּעוֹלָ֑ה וְנָתַתִּ֤י פְעֻלָּתָם֙ בֶּאֱמֶ֔ת וּבְרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם אֶכְר֥וֹת לָהֶֽם׃
Their offspring will be known among the nations, and their descendants among the peoples. All who see them will recognize that they are offspring the LORD has blessed.
וְנוֹדַ֤ע בַּגּוֹיִם֙ זַרְעָ֔ם וְצֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֖ם בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעַמִּ֑ים כָּל־רֹֽאֵיהֶם֙ יַכִּיר֔וּם כִּ֛י הֵ֥ם זֶ֖רַע בֵּרַ֥ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ ס

I will greatly rejoice in the LORD; my soul will exult in my God. For he has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom puts on a garland like a priest,[^12] and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה תָּגֵ֤ל נַפְשִׁי֙ בֵּֽאלֹהַ֔י כִּ֤י הִלְבִּישַׁ֙נִי֙ בִּגְדֵי־יֶ֔שַׁע מְעִ֥יל צְדָקָ֖ה יְעָטָ֑נִי כֶּֽחָתָן֙ יְכַהֵ֣ן פְּאֵ֔ר וְכַכַּלָּ֖ה תַּעְדֶּ֥ה כֵלֶֽיהָ׃
For as the earth brings out its sprouts, and as a garden makes what is sown in it spring up, so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations.
כִּ֤י כָאָ֙רֶץ֙ תּוֹצִ֣יא צִמְחָ֔הּ וּכְגַנָּ֖ה זֵרוּעֶ֣יהָ תַצְמִ֑יחַ כֵּ֣ן ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה יַצְמִ֤יחַ צְדָקָה֙ וּתְהִלָּ֔ה נֶ֖גֶד כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

n.1: Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, wind, breath". Also in verse 3, "spirit".
n.2: *The Lord GOD*: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". God's personal name, YHWH, is written GOD in capitals after "Lord", and "the LORD" elsewhere, as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *mashach*, "anoint", the verb from which *mashiach*, "anointed one" (45:1), comes. Kings and priests were anointed with oil; here the speaker is anointed by the Spirit for his task. The speaker is not named; he may be the prophet or the servant of the earlier chapters (42:1; 48:16; 50:4). In Luke 4:16–21 Jesus reads verses 1–2 in the synagogue at Nazareth, mostly from the Septuagint, and says, "Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing." He stops before "and the day of vengeance of our God".
n.4: Hebrew *basar*, "bring good news" (40:9; 52:7).
n.5: Hebrew *deror*, "release, liberty", the word used for the release proclaimed in the year of Jubilee (Leviticus 25:10).
n.6: Hebrew *peqach-qoach*, probably "opening", that is, the opening of the prison, or of eyes long in darkness. The Septuagint reads "and recovery of sight to the blind", the reading in Luke 4:18, which also adds "to set the oppressed free" from 58:6.
n.7: The *year of favor* recalls the Jubilee year (Leviticus 25:8–17), and the *day of vengeance* is the day when God puts things right (34:8; 63:4).
n.8: A play on words: *pe'er*, "headdress, garland", and *efer*, "ashes", which mourners put on their heads (2 Samuel 13:19).
n.9: Compare Exodus 19:6: "You will be to me a kingdom of priests."
n.10: The Hebrew moves from "you" to "they" in this verse.
n.11: The vowels of the Hebrew text read "robbery with a burnt offering", that is, offerings brought from stolen goods. The same consonants can be read *avlah*, "wrongdoing", as the Septuagint understood them.
n.12: Literally "as a bridegroom acts as priest with a headdress", wearing a garland like the turban of a priest.

v: For the sake of Zion I will not keep silent, and for the sake of Jerusalem I will not rest, until her righteousness[^1] goes out like brightness, and her salvation like a burning torch.
לְמַ֤עַן צִיּוֹן֙ לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה וּלְמַ֥עַן יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט עַד־יֵצֵ֤א כַנֹּ֙גַהּ֙ צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ כְּלַפִּ֥יד יִבְעָֽר׃
The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory. You will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD[^2] will give you.[^3]
וְרָא֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ צִדְקֵ֔ךְ וְכָל־מְלָכִ֖ים כְּבוֹדֵ֑ךְ וְקֹ֤רָא לָךְ֙ שֵׁ֣ם חָדָ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֛ר פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִקֳּבֶֽנּוּ׃
You will be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, a royal diadem in the palm of your God.
וְהָיִ֛יתְ עֲטֶ֥רֶת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת בְּיַד־יְהוָ֑ה *וצנוף **וּצְנִ֥יף מְלוּכָ֖ה בְּכַף־אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃

You will no longer be called Abandoned, and your land will no longer be called Desolate. But you will be called My Delight Is in Her, and your land Married;[^4] for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
לֹֽא־יֵאָמֵר֩ לָ֨ךְ ע֜וֹד עֲזוּבָ֗ה וּלְאַרְצֵךְ֙ לֹא־יֵאָמֵ֥ר עוֹד֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה כִּ֣י לָ֗ךְ יִקָּרֵא֙ חֶפְצִי־בָ֔הּ וּלְאַרְצֵ֖ךְ בְּעוּלָ֑ה כִּֽי־חָפֵ֤ץ יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔ךְ וְאַרְצֵ֖ךְ תִּבָּעֵֽל׃
For as a young man marries a young woman, so your sons will marry you;[^5] and as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
כִּֽי־יִבְעַ֤ל בָּחוּר֙ בְּתוּלָ֔ה יִבְעָל֖וּךְ בָּנָ֑יִךְ וּמְשׂ֤וֹשׂ חָתָן֙ עַל־כַּלָּ֔ה יָשִׂ֥ישׂ עָלַ֖יִךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
On your walls, Jerusalem, I have posted watchmen; all day and all night they will never be silent. You who call on the LORD to remember,[^6] take no rest for yourselves,
עַל־חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הִפְקַ֙דְתִּי֙ שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים כָּל־הַיּ֧וֹם וְכָל־הַלַּ֛יְלָה תָּמִ֖יד לֹ֣א יֶחֱשׁ֑וּ הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה אַל־דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם׃
and give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it the praise of the earth.
וְאַֽל־תִּתְּנ֥וּ דֳמִ֖י ל֑וֹ עַד־יְכוֹנֵ֞ן וְעַד־יָשִׂ֧ים אֶת־יְרֽוּשָׁלַ֛͏ִם תְּהִלָּ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

The LORD has sworn by his right hand and by his mighty arm: I will never again give your grain as food to your enemies, and foreigners will never again drink the new wine for which you have labored.[^7]
נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה בִּֽימִינ֖וֹ וּבִזְר֣וֹעַ עֻזּ֑וֹ אִם־אֶתֵּן֩ אֶת־דְּגָנֵ֨ךְ ע֤וֹד מַֽאֲכָל֙ לְאֹ֣יְבַ֔יִךְ וְאִם־יִשְׁתּ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־נֵכָר֙ תִּֽירוֹשֵׁ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגַ֖עַתְּ בּֽוֹ׃
But those who harvest it will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.
כִּ֤י מְאַסְפָיו֙ יֹאכְלֻ֔הוּ וְהִֽלְל֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וּֽמְקַבְּצָ֥יו יִשְׁתֻּ֖הוּ בְּחַצְר֥וֹת קָדְשִֽׁי׃ ס
Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the way for the people! Build up, build up the highway! Clear it of stones! Raise a signal flag over the peoples!
עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים פַּנּ֖וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָעָ֑ם סֹ֣לּוּ סֹ֤לּוּ הַֽמְסִלָּה֙ סַקְּל֣וּ מֵאֶ֔בֶן הָרִ֥ימוּ נֵ֖ס עַל־הָעַמִּֽים׃
Look, the LORD has proclaimed to the end of the earth: Say to Daughter Zion, "Look, your salvation is coming! Look, his reward is with him, and his recompense goes before him."[^8]
הִנֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה הִשְׁמִ֙יעַ֙ אֶל־קְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ אִמְרוּ֙ לְבַת־צִיּ֔וֹן הִנֵּ֥ה יִשְׁעֵ֖ךְ בָּ֑א הִנֵּ֤ה שְׂכָרוֹ֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וּפְעֻלָּת֖וֹ לְפָנָֽיו׃
They will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the LORD;[^9] and you will be called Sought After, the City Not Abandoned.
וְקָרְא֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם עַם־הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ גְּאוּלֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלָךְ֙ יִקָּרֵ֣א דְרוּשָׁ֔ה עִ֖יר לֹ֥א נֶעֱזָֽבָה׃ ס

n.1: Or "vindication". Hebrew *tsedeq*. Also in verse 2.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "will designate". Compare Revelation 2:17 and 3:12.
n.4: Hebrew *Azuvah*, "Abandoned"; *Shemamah*, "Desolate"; *Cheftsi-vah*, "My Delight Is in Her", traditionally "Hephzibah", the name of King Hezekiah's wife (2 Kings 21:1); *Be'ulah*, "Married", traditionally "Beulah". The verb for "marry" (*ba'al*) also means "become master of" (54:5).
n.5: The same consonants can be read *bonayikh*, "your Builder", a plural form like *bo'alayikh*, "your husband", in 54:5: "so your Builder will marry you".
n.6: Literally "you who cause the LORD to remember", by reminding him in prayer of his promises.
n.7: Literally "If I give … and if foreigners drink …", the form of a solemn oath.
n.8: The words repeat 40:10. Matthew 21:5 joins "Say to Daughter Zion" with Zechariah 9:9.
n.9: Hebrew *ge'ulim*, those whom the LORD has rescued as next of kin (41:14).

v: "Who is this coming from Edom,[^1] in crimson garments from Bozrah,[^2] this one splendid in his clothing, striding forward in the greatness of his strength?" "It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save."[^3]
מִי־זֶ֣ה ׀ בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם חֲמ֤וּץ בְּגָדִים֙ מִבָּצְרָ֔ה זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ צֹעֶ֖ה בְּרֹ֣ב כֹּח֑וֹ אֲנִ֛י מְדַבֵּ֥ר בִּצְדָקָ֖ה רַ֥ב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
"Why is your clothing red, and your garments like those of one who treads in the winepress?"
מַדּ֥וּעַ אָדֹ֖ם לִלְבוּשֶׁ֑ךָ וּבְגָדֶ֖יךָ כְּדֹרֵ֥ךְ בְּגַֽת׃

"I have trodden the winepress alone; from the peoples no one was with me. I trod them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their lifeblood[^4] spattered my garments, and I stained all my clothing.[^5]
פּוּרָ֣ה ׀ דָּרַ֣כְתִּי לְבַדִּ֗י וּמֵֽעַמִּים֙ אֵֽין־אִ֣ישׁ אִתִּ֔י וְאֶדְרְכֵ֣ם בְּאַפִּ֔י וְאֶרְמְסֵ֖ם בַּחֲמָתִ֑י וְיֵ֤ז נִצְחָם֙ עַל־בְּגָדַ֔י וְכָל־מַלְבּוּשַׁ֖י אֶגְאָֽלְתִּי׃
For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption had come.[^6]
כִּ֛י י֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם בְּלִבִּ֑י וּשְׁנַ֥ת גְּאוּלַ֖י בָּֽאָה׃
I looked, but there was no one to help; I was appalled that there was no one to support me. So my own arm brought me salvation, and my fury upheld me.[^7]
וְאַבִּיט֙ וְאֵ֣ין עֹזֵ֔ר וְאֶשְׁתּוֹמֵ֖ם וְאֵ֣ין סוֹמֵ֑ךְ וַתּ֤וֹשַֽׁע לִי֙ זְרֹעִ֔י וַחֲמָתִ֖י הִ֥יא סְמָכָֽתְנִי׃
I trampled the peoples in my anger and made them drunk in my fury, and I poured out their lifeblood on the ground."
וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י וַאֲשַׁכְּרֵ֖ם בַּחֲמָתִ֑י וְאוֹרִ֥יד לָאָ֖רֶץ נִצְחָֽם׃ ס

I will tell of the faithful love[^8] of the LORD,[^9] the praises of the LORD, for all that the LORD has done for us, the great goodness to the house of Israel that he has shown them in his compassion and in his abundant faithful love.
חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה ׀ אַזְכִּיר֙ תְּהִלֹּ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כְּעַ֕ל כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה וְרַב־טוּב֙ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־גְּמָלָ֥ם כְּֽרַחֲמָ֖יו וּכְרֹ֥ב חֲסָדָֽיו׃
He said, "Surely they are my people, children who will not be false." So he became their Savior.
וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַךְ־עַמִּ֣י הֵ֔מָּה בָּנִ֖ים לֹ֣א יְשַׁקֵּ֑רוּ וַיְהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לְמוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
In all their distress he too was distressed,[^10] and the angel of his presence[^11] saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them; he lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
בְּֽכָל־צָרָתָ֣ם ׀ *לא **ל֣וֹ צָ֗ר וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ פָּנָיו֙ הֽוֹשִׁיעָ֔ם בְּאַהֲבָת֥וֹ וּבְחֶמְלָת֖וֹ ה֣וּא גְאָלָ֑ם וַֽיְנַטְּלֵ֥ם וַֽיְנַשְּׂאֵ֖ם כָּל־יְמֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃
But they rebelled and grieved his holy Spirit.[^12] So he turned and became their enemy; he himself fought against them.
וְהֵ֛מָּה מָר֥וּ וְעִצְּב֖וּ אֶת־ר֣וּחַ קָדְשׁ֑וֹ וַיֵּהָפֵ֥ךְ לָהֶ֛ם לְאוֹיֵ֖ב ה֥וּא נִלְחַם־בָּֽם׃
Then his people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses:[^13] Where is he who brought them up out of the sea, with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who put his holy Spirit among them,
וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר יְמֵֽי־עוֹלָ֖ם מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַמּ֑וֹ אַיֵּ֣ה ׀ הַֽמַּעֲלֵ֣ם מִיָּ֗ם אֵ֚ת רֹעֵ֣י צֹאנ֔וֹ אַיֵּ֛ה הַשָּׂ֥ם בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ אֶת־ר֥וּחַ קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
who sent his glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses, who split the waters before them to make for himself an everlasting name,
מוֹלִיךְ֙ לִימִ֣ין מֹשֶׁ֔ה זְר֖וֹעַ תִּפְאַרְתּ֑וֹ בּ֤וֹקֵֽעַ מַ֙יִם֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ל֖וֹ שֵׁ֥ם עוֹלָֽם׃
who led them through the depths? Like a horse in the wilderness, they did not stumble.
מוֹלִיכָ֖ם בַּתְּהֹמ֑וֹת כַּסּ֥וּס בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר לֹ֥א יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ׃
Like cattle that go down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest.[^14] So you led your people, to make for yourself a glorious name.
כַּבְּהֵמָה֙ בַּבִּקְעָ֣ה תֵרֵ֔ד ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה תְּנִיחֶ֑נּוּ כֵּ֚ן נִהַ֣גְתָּ עַמְּךָ֔ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְךָ֖ שֵׁ֥ם תִּפְאָֽרֶת׃
Look down from heaven and see, from your holy and glorious dwelling. Where are your zeal and your mighty deeds? The yearning of your heart[^15] and your compassion are held back from me.
הַבֵּ֤ט מִשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מִזְּבֻ֥ל קָדְשְׁךָ֖ וְתִפְאַרְתֶּ֑ךָ אַיֵּ֤ה קִנְאֽ͏ָתְךָ֙ וּגְב֣וּרֹתֶ֔ךָ הֲמ֥וֹן מֵעֶ֛יךָ וְֽרַחֲמֶ֖יךָ אֵלַ֥י הִתְאַפָּֽקוּ׃
For you are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, LORD, are our Father; "Our Redeemer from of old" is your name.[^16]
כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה אָבִ֔ינוּ כִּ֤י אַבְרָהָם֙ לֹ֣א יְדָעָ֔נוּ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֣א יַכִּירָ֑נוּ אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אָבִ֔ינוּ גֹּאֲלֵ֥נוּ מֵֽעוֹלָ֖ם שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
Why, LORD, do you make us wander from your ways and harden our hearts so that we do not fear you? Return for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance.
לָ֣מָּה תַתְעֵ֤נוּ יְהוָה֙ מִדְּרָכֶ֔יךָ תַּקְשִׁ֥יחַ לִבֵּ֖נוּ מִיִּרְאָתֶ֑ךָ שׁ֚וּב לְמַ֣עַן עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ שִׁבְטֵ֖י נַחֲלָתֶֽךָ׃
Your holy people possessed it for only a little while;[^17] our adversaries have trampled down your sanctuary.
לַמִּצְעָ֕ר יָרְשׁ֖וּ עַם־קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ צָרֵ֕ינוּ בּוֹסְס֖וּ מִקְדָּשֶֽׁךָ׃

We have become like those you have never ruled, like those who were never called by your name. If only you would tear open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains would quake at your presence![^18]
הָיִ֗ינוּ מֵֽעוֹלָם֙ לֹֽא־מָשַׁ֣לְתָּ בָּ֔ם לֹֽא־נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם לוּא־קָרַ֤עְתָּ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ יָרַ֔דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ׃

n.1: The land south and east of the Dead Sea (34:5–6). *Edom* sounds like *adom*, "red" (verse 2).
n.2: The chief city of Edom (34:6). *Crimson* is literally "stained" or "bright red".
n.3: The speaker who comes from Edom is the LORD, and in verses 1–6 the prophet's questions and the LORD's answers alternate.
n.4: Hebrew *netsach*, here "juice, lifeblood", the red juice of the grapes. Also in verse 6.
n.5: Revelation 14:19–20 and 19:13–15 echo verses 1–6.
n.6: Or "the year of my redeemed ones had come". Hebrew *ge'ulai*.
n.7: Compare 59:16.
n.8: Hebrew *chasdei*, the plural of *chesed*, "acts of faithful love". Also at the end of the verse.
n.9: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.10: Literally "to him was distress". The Hebrew text is written *lo*, "not", but read *lo*, "to him": the written text may mean "In all their distress he did not afflict them". The Septuagint reads "not an envoy or an angel, but he himself saved them".
n.11: Literally "the angel of his face". Or "the messenger of his presence". Compare Exodus 23:20–23; 33:14–15.
n.12: Literally "the spirit of his holiness" (Psalm 51:13; 51:11 in most English Bibles). Also in verse 11. Ephesians 4:30 echoes this line.
n.13: Literally "And he remembered the days of old, Moses, his people". The Hebrew is difficult.
n.14: Literally "gave him rest", that is, gave rest to the people.
n.15: Literally "the stirring of your inner parts".
n.16: Hebrew *go'el* (41:14).
n.17: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "For a little while they possessed your holy people".
n.18: The second half of this verse, "If only you would tear open the heavens …", is 64:1 in most English Bibles, and 64:1–11 are 64:2–12. Compare Judges 5:5 and Psalm 18:10 (18:9 in most English Bibles).

v: As when fire kindles brushwood, and fire makes water boil, make your name known to your adversaries, so that the nations may tremble at your presence![^1]
כִּקְדֹ֧חַ אֵ֣שׁ הֲמָסִ֗ים מַ֚יִם תִּבְעֶה־אֵ֔שׁ לְהוֹדִ֥יעַ שִׁמְךָ֖ לְצָרֶ֑יךָ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ גּוֹיִ֥ם יִרְגָּֽזוּ׃
When you did awesome things that we did not expect, you came down; the mountains quaked at your presence.
בַּעֲשׂוֹתְךָ֥ נוֹרָא֖וֹת לֹ֣א נְקַוֶּ֑ה יָרַ֕דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ׃
From ages past no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides you, who acts for those who wait for him.[^2]
וּמֵעוֹלָ֥ם לֹא־שָׁמְע֖וּ לֹ֣א הֶאֱזִ֑ינוּ עַ֣יִן לֹֽא־רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔ יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לִמְחַכֵּה־לֽוֹ׃
You meet those who gladly do what is right, who remember you in your ways. Look, you were angry, and we sinned. We have been in them a long time; can we be saved?[^3]
פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת־שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ הֵן־אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֙פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א בָּהֶ֥ם עוֹלָ֖ם וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעַ׃
We have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like a filthy cloth.[^4] We all wither like a leaf, and our wrongdoings carry us away like the wind.
וַנְּהִ֤י כַטָּמֵא֙ כֻּלָּ֔נוּ וּכְבֶ֥גֶד עִדִּ֖ים כָּל־צִדְקֹתֵ֑ינוּ וַנָּ֤בֶל כֶּֽעָלֶה֙ כֻּלָּ֔נוּ וַעֲוֺנֵ֖נוּ כָּר֥וּחַ יִשָּׂאֻֽנוּ׃
No one calls on your name or rouses himself to take hold of you. For you have hidden your face from us and made us melt away in the grip of our wrongdoings.[^5]
וְאֵין־קוֹרֵ֣א בְשִׁמְךָ֔ מִתְעוֹרֵ֖ר לְהַחֲזִ֣יק בָּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־הִסְתַּ֤רְתָּ פָנֶ֙יךָ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וַתְּמוּגֵ֖נוּ בְּיַד־עֲוֺנֵֽנוּ׃
But now, LORD,[^6] you are our Father. We are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
וְעַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אָבִ֣ינוּ אָ֑תָּה אֲנַ֤חְנוּ הַחֹ֙מֶר֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה יֹצְרֵ֔נוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדְךָ֖ כֻּלָּֽנוּ׃
Do not be so very angry, LORD, and do not remember our wrongdoing forever. Look, please, we are all your people.
אַל־תִּקְצֹ֤ף יְהוָה֙ עַד־מְאֹ֔ד וְאַל־לָעַ֖ד תִּזְכֹּ֣ר עָוֺ֑ן הֵ֥ן הַבֶּט־נָ֖א עַמְּךָ֥ כֻלָּֽנוּ׃
Your holy cities have become a wilderness; Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
עָרֵ֥י קָדְשְׁךָ֖ הָי֣וּ מִדְבָּ֑ר צִיּוֹן֙ מִדְבָּ֣ר הָיָ֔תָה יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם שְׁמָמָֽה׃
Our holy and beautiful house, where our ancestors praised you, has been burned with fire, and all that we treasured has become ruins.[^7]
בֵּ֧ית קָדְשֵׁ֣נוּ וְתִפְאַרְתֵּ֗נוּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִֽלְל֙וּךָ֙ אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ הָיָ֖ה לִשְׂרֵ֣פַת אֵ֑שׁ וְכָל־מַחֲמַדֵּ֖ינוּ הָיָ֥ה לְחָרְבָּֽה׃
After all this, LORD, will you hold back? Will you keep silent and afflict us so very much?
הַעַל־אֵ֥לֶּה תִתְאַפַּ֖ק יְהוָ֑ה תֶּחֱשֶׁ֥ה וּתְעַנֵּ֖נוּ עַד־מְאֹֽד׃ ס

n.1: Verses 1–11 are 64:2–12 in most English Bibles. The prayer that began in 63:15 continues to the end of this chapter. *Brushwood* is Hebrew *hamasim*, a word found only here.
n.2: Paul echoes this verse in 1 Corinthians 2:9: "What no eye has seen, nor ear heard … God has prepared for those who love him."
n.3: The Hebrew of the last line is very difficult. Literally "in them forever, and we will be saved". *Them* may be the LORD's ways or the people's sins. Some take the line as a statement: "In them we will be saved forever."
n.4: Literally "a garment of menstruation", a cloth made unclean by menstrual blood (Leviticus 15:19–24).
n.5: Literally "made us melt in the hand of our wrongdoings".
n.6: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.7: Literally "all our precious things have become a ruin", perhaps the city's treasured places or the temple's treasures. The temple was burned by the Babylonians in 587 or 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9).

v: I let myself be sought by those who did not ask for me; I let myself be found by those who did not seek me. I said, "Here I am, here I am," to a nation that was not called by my name.[^1]
נִדְרַ֙שְׁתִּי֙ לְל֣וֹא שָׁאָ֔לוּ נִמְצֵ֖אתִי לְלֹ֣א בִקְשֻׁ֑נִי אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ הִנֵּ֣נִי הִנֵּ֔נִי אֶל־גּ֖וֹי לֹֽא־קֹרָ֥א בִשְׁמִֽי׃
All day long I have held out my hands to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, following their own thoughts,
פֵּרַ֧שְׂתִּי יָדַ֛י כָּל־הַיּ֖וֹם אֶל־עַ֣ם סוֹרֵ֑ר הַהֹלְכִים֙ הַדֶּ֣רֶךְ לֹא־ט֔וֹב אַחַ֖ר מַחְשְׁבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens and burning incense on bricks,[^2]
הָעָ֗ם הַמַּכְעִיסִ֥ים אוֹתִ֛י עַל־פָּנַ֖י תָּמִ֑יד זֹֽבְחִים֙ בַּגַּנּ֔וֹת וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים עַל־הַלְּבֵנִֽים׃
who sit among the graves and spend the night in secret places,[^3] who eat the flesh of pigs, with broth of spoiled meat[^4] in their pots,
הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בַּקְּבָרִ֔ים וּבַנְּצוּרִ֖ים יָלִ֑ינוּ הָאֹֽכְלִים֙ בְּשַׂ֣ר הַחֲזִ֔יר *ופרק **וּמְרַ֥ק פִּגֻּלִ֖ים כְּלֵיהֶֽם׃
who say, "Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am too holy for you!"[^5] These are smoke in my nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.
הָאֹֽמְרִים֙ קְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־תִּגַּשׁ־בִּ֖י כִּ֣י קְדַשְׁתִּ֑יךָ אֵ֚לֶּה עָשָׁ֣ן בְּאַפִּ֔י אֵ֥שׁ יֹקֶ֖דֶת כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
Look, it is written before me: I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will repay into their laps[^6]
הִנֵּ֥ה כְתוּבָ֖ה לְפָנָ֑י לֹ֤א אֶחֱשֶׂה֙ כִּ֣י אִם־שִׁלַּ֔מְתִּי וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֖י עַל־חֵיקָֽם׃

both your wrongdoings and the wrongdoings of your ancestors together,[^7] says the LORD,[^8] because they burned incense on the mountains and insulted me on the hills. I will measure into their laps full payment for their former deeds.[^9]
עֲ֠וֺנֹתֵיכֶם וַעֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֤ם יַחְדָּו֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ֙ עַל־הֶ֣הָרִ֔ים וְעַל־הַגְּבָע֖וֹת חֵרְפ֑וּנִי וּמַדֹּתִ֧י פְעֻלָּתָ֛ם רִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה *על־**אֶל־חֵיקָֽם׃ ס

This is what the LORD says: As when new wine is found in a cluster of grapes and someone says, "Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it,"[^10] so I will do for the sake of my servants, so as not to destroy them all.
כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֤א הַתִּירוֹשׁ֙ בָּֽאֶשְׁכּ֔וֹל וְאָמַר֙ אַל־תַּשְׁחִיתֵ֔הוּ כִּ֥י בְרָכָ֖ה בּ֑וֹ כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ לְמַ֣עַן עֲבָדַ֔י לְבִלְתִּ֖י הֽ͏ַשְׁחִ֥ית הַכֹּֽל׃
I will bring out offspring from Jacob, and from Judah heirs to my mountains. My chosen ones will possess them, and my servants will live there.
וְהוֹצֵאתִ֤י מִֽיַּעֲקֹב֙ זֶ֔רַע וּמִיהוּדָ֖ה יוֹרֵ֣שׁ הָרָ֑י וִירֵשׁ֣וּהָ בְחִירַ֔י וַעֲבָדַ֖י יִשְׁכְּנוּ־שָֽׁמָּה׃
Sharon will become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor[^11] a resting place for herds, for my people who have sought me.
וְהָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ לִנְוֵה־צֹ֔אן וְעֵ֥מֶק עָכ֖וֹר לְרֵ֣בֶץ בָּקָ֑ר לְעַמִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר דְּרָשֽׁוּנִי׃
But you who abandon the LORD, who forget my holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny,[^12]
וְאַתֶּם֙ עֹזְבֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הַשְּׁכֵחִ֖ים אֶת־הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֑י הֽ͏ַעֹרְכִ֤ים לַגַּד֙ שֻׁלְחָ֔ן וְהַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים לַמְנִ֥י מִמְסָֽךְ׃

I will destine you for the sword,[^13] and all of you will bow down to be slaughtered, because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen. You did what was evil in my eyes and chose what does not please me.

וּמָנִ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֜ם לַחֶ֗רֶב וְכֻלְּכֶם֙ לַטֶּ֣בַח תִּכְרָ֔עוּ יַ֤עַן קָרָ֙אתִי֙ וְלֹ֣א עֲנִיתֶ֔ם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם וַתַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־חָפַ֖צְתִּי בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃ פ

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Look, my servants will eat, but you will go hungry; look, my servants will drink, but you will go thirsty; look, my servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.
לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤י ׀ יֹאכֵ֙לוּ֙ וְאַתֶּ֣ם תִּרְעָ֔בוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יִשְׁתּ֖וּ וְאַתֶּ֣ם תִּצְמָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יִשְׂמָ֖חוּ וְאַתֶּ֥ם תֵּבֹֽשׁוּ׃
Look, my servants will sing for joy with gladness of heart, but you will cry out with pain of heart and wail with a broken spirit.
הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יָרֹ֖נּוּ מִטּ֣וּב לֵ֑ב וְאַתֶּ֤ם תִּצְעֲקוּ֙ מִכְּאֵ֣ב לֵ֔ב וּמִשֵּׁ֥בֶר ר֖וּחַ תְּיֵלִֽילוּ׃
You will leave your name to my chosen ones as a curse,[^14] and the Lord GOD will put you to death, but he will call his servants by another name.
וְהִנַּחְתֶּ֨ם שִׁמְכֶ֤ם לִשְׁבוּעָה֙ לִבְחִירַ֔י וֶהֱמִיתְ֖ךָ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְלַעֲבָדָ֥יו יִקְרָ֖א שֵׁ֥ם אַחֵֽר׃

So whoever invokes a blessing in the land will be blessed by the God of truth,[^15] and whoever swears an oath in the land will swear by the God of truth. For the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from my eyes.
אֲשֶׁ֨ר הַמִּתְבָּרֵ֜ךְ בָּאָ֗רֶץ יִתְבָּרֵךְ֙ בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י אָמֵ֔ן וְהַנִּשְׁבָּ֣ע בָּאָ֔רֶץ יִשָּׁבַ֖ע בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י אָמֵ֑ן כִּ֣י נִשְׁכְּח֗וּ הַצָּרוֹת֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת וְכִ֥י נִסְתְּר֖וּ מֵעֵינָֽי׃
For look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered or come to mind.[^16]
כִּֽי־הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִזָּכַ֙רְנָה֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת וְלֹ֥א תַעֲלֶ֖ינָה עַל־לֵֽב׃
But be glad and rejoice forever in what I am creating, for look, I am creating Jerusalem to be a delight and its people a joy.
כִּֽי־אִם־שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְגִ֙ילוּ֙ עֲדֵי־עַ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י בוֹרֵ֑א כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י בוֹרֵ֧א אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֛͏ִם גִּילָ֖ה וְעַמָּ֥הּ מָשֽׂוֹשׂ׃
I will rejoice over Jerusalem and delight in my people; the sound of weeping and the sound of crying will no longer be heard in it.[^17]
וְגַלְתִּ֥י בִירוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם וְשַׂשְׂתִּ֣י בְעַמִּ֑י וְלֹֽא־יִשָּׁמַ֥ע בָּהּ֙ ע֔וֹד ק֥וֹל בְּכִ֖י וְק֥וֹל זְעָקָֽה׃

There will no longer be in it an infant who lives only a few days, or an old man who does not live out his days. For one who dies at a hundred years will be thought a youth, and one who falls short of a hundred years will be thought accursed.[^18]
לֹא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה מִשָּׁ֜ם ע֗וֹד ע֤וּל יָמִים֙ וְזָקֵ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יְמַלֵּ֖א אֶת־יָמָ֑יו כִּ֣י הַנַּ֗עַר בֶּן־מֵאָ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יָמ֔וּת וְהַ֣חוֹטֶ֔א בֶּן־מֵאָ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה יְקֻלָּֽל׃
They will build houses and live in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
וּבָנ֥וּ בָתִּ֖ים וְיָשָׁ֑בוּ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְאָכְל֖וּ פִּרְיָֽם׃
They will not build for others to live in, or plant for others to eat. For like the days of a tree will be the days of my people, and my chosen ones will long enjoy the work of their hands.
לֹ֤א יִבְנוּ֙ וְאַחֵ֣ר יֵשֵׁ֔ב לֹ֥א יִטְּע֖וּ וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל כִּֽי־כִימֵ֤י הָעֵץ֙ יְמֵ֣י עַמִּ֔י וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶ֖ם יְבַלּ֥וּ בְחִירָֽי׃
They will not labor in vain or bear children for sudden disaster, for they will be offspring blessed by the LORD, and their descendants with them.
לֹ֤א יִֽיגְעוּ֙ לָרִ֔יק וְלֹ֥א יֵלְד֖וּ לַבֶּהָלָ֑ה כִּ֣י זֶ֜רַע בְּרוּכֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ הֵ֔מָּה וְצֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֖ם אִתָּֽם׃
Before they call, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.
וְהָיָ֥ה טֶֽרֶם־יִקְרָ֖אוּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶעֱנֶ֑ה ע֛וֹד הֵ֥ם מְדַבְּרִ֖ים וַאֲנִ֥י אֶשְׁמָֽע׃
The wolf and the lamb will graze together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, and dust will be the serpent's food.[^19] They will not harm or destroy on all my holy mountain, says the LORD.
זְאֵ֨ב וְטָלֶ֜ה יִרְע֣וּ כְאֶחָ֗ד וְאַרְיֵה֙ כַּבָּקָ֣ר יֹֽאכַל־תֶּ֔בֶן וְנָחָ֖שׁ עָפָ֣ר לַחְמ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יָרֵ֧עוּ וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁחִ֛יתוּ בְּכָל־הַ֥ר קָדְשִׁ֖י אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ ס

n.1: Or "to a nation that did not call on my name", as the Septuagint reads. Romans 10:20–21 quotes verses 1–2 from the Septuagint, applying verse 1 to the nations and verse 2 to Israel.
n.2: Perhaps altars or tiles of brick used in the worship of other gods.
n.3: Hebrew *netsurim*, "guarded places", perhaps tombs or caves where people sought messages from the dead.
n.4: Hebrew *piggulim*, "foul, rotten": meat unfit to eat and offensive to God (Leviticus 7:18). The Hebrew text is written "pieces" but read "broth".
n.5: Literally "for I am holy to you", or perhaps "for I would make you holy", that is, by contact, as holy things passed on their holiness (Ezekiel 44:19).
n.6: Literally "into their bosom", the fold of the garment over the chest. Also in verse 7.
n.7: The Hebrew moves from "their" in verse 6 to "your" here and back to "their".
n.8: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.9: Literally "I will measure their work first into their bosom". Or "I will measure out their payment in full".
n.10: Perhaps the words of a song sung at the grape harvest. Psalms 57–59 and 75 are set to a tune called "Do Not Destroy".
n.11: A valley near Jericho, named for the "trouble" (*akhar*) brought on Israel by Achan (Joshua 7:24–26). Hosea 2:17 (2:15 in most English Bibles) promises that it will become "a door of hope".
n.12: Hebrew *Gad* and *Meni*, gods of good fortune and fate, honored with meals and drink offerings.
n.13: A play on words: *u-maniti*, "I will destine", and *Meni*, "Destiny", in verse 11.
n.14: Hebrew *shevu'ah*, "oath", here a formula for cursing: their name will be used in the words "May the LORD make you like …" (compare Jeremiah 29:22). *You* in the next line is singular.
n.15: Literally "the God of Amen". *Amen* means "firm, sure, true". Compare Revelation 3:14, where Jesus is called "the Amen".
n.16: 2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1 take up the promise of new heavens and a new earth (also 66:22).
n.17: Revelation 21:4 echoes this line.
n.18: Or "and the sinner who reaches a hundred years will be accursed". Hebrew *ha-chote* means "the sinner" or "one who misses the mark".
n.19: The serpent's curse in Genesis 3:14. Verse 25 repeats parts of 11:6–9.

v: This is what the LORD[^1] says: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. Where is the house you would build for me? Where is the place of my rest?
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם כִּסְאִ֔י וְהָאָ֖רֶץ הֲדֹ֣ם רַגְלָ֑י אֵי־זֶ֥ה בַ֙יִת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּבְנוּ־לִ֔י וְאֵי־זֶ֥ה מָק֖וֹם מְנוּחָתִֽי׃
My hand made all these things, and so they came to be,[^2] declares the LORD. But this is the one I will look to: the one who is humble and contrite in spirit, and who trembles at my word.
וְאֶת־כָּל־אֵ֙לֶּה֙ יָדִ֣י עָשָׂ֔תָה וַיִּהְי֥וּ כָל־אֵ֖לֶּה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶל־זֶ֣ה אַבִּ֔יט אֶל־עָנִי֙ וּנְכֵה־ר֔וּחַ וְחָרֵ֖ד עַל־דְּבָרִֽי׃

Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who kills a person; whoever sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog's neck; whoever presents a grain offering, like one who offers pig's blood; whoever burns incense as a memorial, like one who blesses an idol.[^3] They have chosen their own ways, and they delight in their detestable things.[^4]

שׁוֹחֵ֨ט הַשּׁ֜וֹר מַכֵּה־אִ֗ישׁ זוֹבֵ֤חַ הַשֶּׂה֙ עֹ֣רֵֽף כֶּ֔לֶב מַעֲלֵ֤ה מִנְחָה֙ דַּם־חֲזִ֔יר מַזְכִּ֥יר לְבֹנָ֖ה מְבָ֣רֵֽךְ אָ֑וֶן גַּם־הֵ֗מָּה בָּֽחֲרוּ֙ בְּדַרְכֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְשִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֖ם נַפְשָׁ֥ם חָפֵֽצָה׃

So I too will choose harsh treatment for them and bring on them what they dread. For I called, and no one answered; I spoke, and they did not listen. They did what was evil in my eyes and chose what does not please me.[^5]

גַּם־אֲנִ֞י אֶבְחַ֣ר בְּתַעֲלֻלֵיהֶ֗ם וּמְגֽוּרֹתָם֙ אָבִ֣יא לָהֶ֔ם יַ֤עַן קָרָ֙אתִי֙ וְאֵ֣ין עוֹנֶ֔ה דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־חָפַ֖צְתִּי בָּחָֽרוּ׃ ס

Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at his word: Your brothers who hate you and cast you out for my name's sake have said, "Let the LORD show his glory, so that we may see your joy!" But they will be put to shame.
שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה הַחֲרֵדִ֖ים אֶל־דְּבָר֑וֹ אָמְרוּ֩ אֲחֵיכֶ֨ם שֹׂנְאֵיכֶ֜ם מְנַדֵּיכֶ֗ם לְמַ֤עַן שְׁמִי֙ יִכְבַּ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה וְנִרְאֶ֥ה בְשִׂמְחַתְכֶ֖ם וְהֵ֥ם יֵבֹֽשׁוּ׃
Listen! An uproar from the city! A sound from the temple! It is the sound of the LORD repaying his enemies what they deserve.
ק֤וֹל שָׁאוֹן֙ מֵעִ֔יר ק֖וֹל מֵֽהֵיכָ֑ל ק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁלֵּ֥ם גְּמ֖וּל לְאֹיְבָֽיו׃
Before she went into labor, she gave birth; before her pains came on her, she delivered a son.
בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּחִ֖יל יָלָ֑דָה בְּטֶ֨רֶם יָב֥וֹא חֵ֛בֶל לָ֖הּ וְהִמְלִ֥יטָה זָכָֽר׃
Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen such things? Can a land be born in one day, or a nation be brought forth in a moment? Yet as soon as Zion went into labor, she gave birth to her children.
מִֽי־שָׁמַ֣ע כָּזֹ֗את מִ֤י רָאָה֙ כָּאֵ֔לֶּה הֲי֤וּחַל אֶ֙רֶץ֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד אִם־יִוָּ֥לֵֽד גּ֖וֹי פַּ֣עַם אֶחָ֑ת כִּֽי־חָ֛לָה גַּם־יָלְדָ֥ה צִיּ֖וֹן אֶת־בָּנֶֽיהָ׃
Shall I bring to the moment of birth[^6] and not cause delivery? says the LORD. Shall I, who cause delivery, close the womb? says your God.
הַאֲנִ֥י אַשְׁבִּ֛יר וְלֹ֥א אוֹלִ֖יד יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־אֲנִ֧י הַמּוֹלִ֛יד וְעָצַ֖רְתִּי אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃ ס
Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad for her, all you who love her! Rejoice greatly with her, all you who mourn over her,
שִׂמְח֧וּ אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֛͏ִם וְגִ֥ילוּ בָ֖הּ כָּל־אֹהֲבֶ֑יהָ שִׂ֤ישׂוּ אִתָּהּ֙ מָשׂ֔וֹשׂ כָּל־הַמִּֽתְאַבְּלִ֖ים עָלֶֽיהָ׃
so that you may nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts, so that you may drink deeply and delight in her overflowing abundance.[^7]
לְמַ֤עַן תִּֽינְקוּ֙ וּשְׂבַעְתֶּ֔ם מִשֹּׁ֖ד תַּנְחֻמֶ֑יהָ לְמַ֧עַן תָּמֹ֛צּוּ וְהִתְעַנַּגְתֶּ֖ם מִזִּ֥יז כְּבוֹדָֽהּ׃ ס

For this is what the LORD says: Look, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the wealth of the nations like an overflowing stream. You will nurse and be carried on her hip and bounced on her knees.
כִּֽי־כֹ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִ֣י נֹטֶֽה־אֵ֠לֶיהָ כְּנָהָ֨ר שָׁל֜וֹם וּכְנַ֧חַל שׁוֹטֵ֛ף כְּב֥וֹד גּוֹיִ֖ם וִֽינַקְתֶּ֑ם עַל־צַד֙ תִּנָּשֵׂ֔אוּ וְעַל־בִּרְכַּ֖יִם תְּשָׁעֳשָֽׁעוּ׃
As a mother comforts her child,[^8] so I will comfort you; you will be comforted in Jerusalem.
כְּאִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִמּ֖וֹ תְּנַחֲמֶ֑נּוּ כֵּ֤ן אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֲנַ֣חֶמְכֶ֔ם וּבִירֽוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם תְּנֻחָֽמוּ׃
You will see, and your heart will rejoice; your bones will flourish like grass. The hand of the LORD will be made known to his servants, but his fury to his enemies.
וּרְאִיתֶם֙ וְשָׂ֣שׂ לִבְּכֶ֔ם וְעַצְמוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם כַּדֶּ֣שֶׁא תִפְרַ֑חְנָה וְנוֹדְעָ֤ה יַד־יְהוָה֙ אֶת־עֲבָדָ֔יו וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת־אֹיְבָֽיו׃
For look, the LORD will come in fire, and his chariots like the whirlwind, to repay his anger with fury and his rebuke with flames of fire.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּאֵ֣שׁ יָב֔וֹא וְכַסּוּפָ֖ה מַרְכְּבֹתָ֑יו לְהָשִׁ֤יב בְּחֵמָה֙ אַפּ֔וֹ וְגַעֲרָת֖וֹ בְּלַהֲבֵי־אֵֽשׁ׃
For with fire the LORD will execute judgment, and with his sword, on all people,[^9] and those slain by the LORD will be many.
כִּ֤י בָאֵשׁ֙ יְהוָ֣ה נִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּבְחַרְבּ֖וֹ אֶת־כָּל־בָּשָׂ֑ר וְרַבּ֖וּ חַֽלְלֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

Those who consecrate and purify themselves to go into the gardens, following one in the middle,[^10] who eat the flesh of pigs and vile things and mice, will come to an end together, declares the LORD.
הַמִּתְקַדְּשִׁ֨ים וְהַמִּֽטַּהֲרִ֜ים אֶל־הַגַּנּ֗וֹת אַחַ֤ר *אחד **אַחַת֙ בַּתָּ֔וֶךְ אֹֽכְלֵי֙ בְּשַׂ֣ר הַחֲזִ֔יר וְהַשֶּׁ֖קֶץ וְהָעַכְבָּ֑ר יַחְדָּ֥ו יָסֻ֖פוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
As for me, I know their deeds and their thoughts, and the time is coming to gather all nations and languages.[^11] They will come and see my glory.
וְאָנֹכִ֗י מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ וּמַחְשְׁבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם בָּאָ֕ה לְקַבֵּ֥ץ אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם וְהַלְּשֹׁנ֑וֹת וּבָ֖אוּ וְרָא֥וּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדִֽי׃

I will set a sign among them, and I will send survivors from them to the nations: to Tarshish, Pul and Lud (who draw the bow), to Tubal and Javan,[^12] to the distant coastlands[^13] that have not heard of my fame or seen my glory. They will declare my glory among the nations.

וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י בָהֶ֜ם א֗וֹת וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֣י מֵהֶ֣ם ׀ פְּ֠לֵיטִים אֶֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֞ם תַּרְשִׁ֨ישׁ פּ֥וּל וְל֛וּד מֹ֥שְׁכֵי קֶ֖שֶׁת תֻּבַ֣ל וְיָוָ֑ן הָאִיִּ֣ים הָרְחֹקִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־שָׁמְע֤וּ אֶת־שִׁמְעִי֙ וְלֹא־רָא֣וּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדִ֔י וְהִגִּ֥ידוּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדִ֖י בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃

They will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering[^14] to the LORD, on horses, in chariots and wagons, on mules and on camels,[^15] to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the Israelites bring a grain offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.

וְהֵבִ֣יאוּ אֶת־כָּל־אֲחֵיכֶ֣ם מִכָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֣ם ׀ מִנְחָ֣ה ׀ לַֽיהוָ֡ה בַּסּוּסִ֡ים וּ֠בָרֶכֶב וּבַצַּבִּ֨ים וּבַפְּרָדִ֜ים וּבַכִּרְכָּר֗וֹת עַ֣ל הַ֥ר קָדְשִׁ֛י יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָבִיאוּ֩ בְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֛ה בִּכְלִ֥י טָה֖וֹר בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
And I will also take some of them to be priests and Levites,[^16] says the LORD.
וְגַם־מֵהֶ֥ם אֶקַּ֛ח לַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים לַלְוִיִּ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
For as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will endure before me, declares the LORD, so your offspring and your name will endure.
כִּ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם הַ֠חֳדָשִׁים וְהָאָ֨רֶץ הַחֲדָשָׁ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֛ה עֹמְדִ֥ים לְפָנַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כֵּ֛ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם וְשִׁמְכֶֽם׃
From new moon to new moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all people will come to bow down before me, says the LORD.
וְהָיָ֗ה מִֽדֵּי־חֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ בְּחָדְשׁ֔וֹ וּמִדֵּ֥י שַׁבָּ֖ת בְּשַׁבַּתּ֑וֹ יָב֧וֹא כָל־בָּשָׂ֛ר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת לְפָנַ֖י אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
They will go out and look on the corpses of the people who rebelled against me. For their worm will not die, and their fire will not be quenched,[^17] and they will be a horror to all people.[^18]
וְיָצְא֣וּ וְרָא֔וּ בְּפִגְרֵי֙ הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַפֹּשְׁעִ֖ים בִּ֑י כִּ֣י תוֹלַעְתָּ֞ם לֹ֣א תָמ֗וּת וְאִשָּׁם֙ לֹ֣א תִכְבֶּ֔ה וְהָי֥וּ דֵרָא֖וֹן לְכָל־בָּשָֽׂר׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Stephen quotes verses 1–2 in Acts 7:49–50.
n.2: The Septuagint reads "and all these things are mine".
n.3: The Hebrew sets each pair side by side without "like": literally "one who slaughters the ox, one who strikes a man; one who sacrifices the lamb, one who breaks a dog's neck …". It may mean that their sacrifices are as unacceptable as murder and unclean offerings, or that the same people who sacrifice also commit these acts. *Idol* is Hebrew *aven*, "wickedness, nothingness" (41:29).
n.4: Literally "their *nephesh* delights in their detestable things". Hebrew *shiqqutsim*, a word for idols and unclean things.
n.5: The last two sentences repeat 65:12.
n.6: Literally "Shall I bring to the breaking point", the word used in 37:3 for the moment of birth.
n.7: Hebrew *ziz*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "abundance" or "breast". Literally "the abundance of her glory".
n.8: Literally "As a man whom his mother comforts".
n.9: Literally "all flesh". Also in verses 23 and 24.
n.10: The Hebrew text is written with a masculine form but read with a feminine form of "one". The leader of the rites in the gardens (65:3) may have been a priest or priestess. The meaning is uncertain.
n.11: The Hebrew is incomplete. Literally "And I, their deeds and their thoughts, coming to gather all the nations and languages". The verb "know" is not in the Hebrew, but is found in the Septuagint. *The time* is supplied: the Hebrew has only the feminine form "is coming".
n.12: Distant peoples. *Tarshish* was a port in the far west (2:16); *Pul* is otherwise unknown as a land, and the Septuagint reads "Put", that is, Libya (Jeremiah 46:9); *Lud* is Lydia in Asia Minor, or a people of Africa; *Tubal* was in eastern Asia Minor; *Javan* is Greece (Ionia). For "who draw the bow" the Septuagint reads "Meshech", another people of Asia Minor (Ezekiel 27:13).
n.13: Hebrew *iyyim*, the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean (11:11), and in these chapters the most distant lands.
n.14: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute", in Leviticus a grain offering, as later in this verse.
n.15: Hebrew *kirkarot*, a word found only here, probably camels or other swift animals.
n.16: *Some of them* may be the nations of verses 18–19 or the brothers they bring back in verse 20.
n.17: Jesus quotes this line in Mark 9:48.
n.18: Hebrew *dera'on*, "horror, abhorrence", found also in Daniel 12:2, of those who will rise "to everlasting contempt". When this chapter is read aloud in the synagogue, verse 23 is repeated after this verse, so that the reading, and the book, do not end on this note. The same is done at the end of Malachi, Lamentations and Ecclesiastes.
